**E63.4 Predictions**

| # | test | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| P237 | ctrl and fix: consensus head in every B net, in no A net (at most one exception in 23) | fails: ctrl 11 of 11 agree; fix 5 exceptions (B nets without a consensus head) |
| P238 | ext: AUC(C_max; B > A) >= 0.90 | holds: 1.00 [1.00, 1.00] (199 nets, 11 clusters) |
| P239 | A nets with two pooling heads: opposite-sign mean K_odd (at most one exception) | holds: 8 of 8 |
| P240 | (a) ctrl: every pooling head L_own > 0 and dlogit < -1; (b) median L_own(own) < 0.5 x ctrl's | holds: (a) 14 of 14 heads; (b) -0.82 against 16.8 |
| P241 | ctrl: KL(orthn) < KL(base) in >= 9 of 11, mean reduction >= 0.03; own: mean change <= 0.02 | holds: 11 of 11, 0.144; own 0.001 |

**What this says.**
- **A and B go with head allocations.** An A net has two block-1 summary heads that pool its source's own errors; a B net has fewer (post hoc, 222 of 222). With random codes, B's other head puts its mass on the three query-question tokens in 137 of 149 cases; with fixed codes it more often goes to other sources' labelled tokens. Every run has a summaries head early (by 2,000 steps, when reliability weighting is acquired, E16), and A runs convert it into a second pooling head at 5,000-20,000 steps, the window in which E47's markers separate the types. With E44 (block 1's initial attention weights carry the type most often) and E43 (the type stays with the initialisation), the type looks like the allocation a net's block-1 heads settle in. That this allocation causes B's larger KL, sign dependence or departure is not tested here.
- **An opposite-sign pair.** In every A net of ctrl and fix (and in every own net) the two pooling heads have opposite signed-numerator coefficients: one head's scores rise with positive errors, the other's with negative ones. A weighted mean of r_j / n_j under scores proportional to beta r_j / n_j carries an even, roughly quadratic statistic of the errors (about beta sum r_j^2 / n_j^2) and is sign-dependent within one head; whether A's pair cancels that dependence downstream, and is why A depends less on the signs (E27: 7% against 25%), is a hypothesis.
- **The routing logit lowers large errors' scores.** In pre-LN attention an error's size enters a key's score only through the LayerNorm norm, scaled by the key's norm-scaled logit L, and through the signed feature. In every standard pooling head L_own is large and positive (the routing score that picks out the source's tokens), so the norm term lowers an own key's score at |r| = 3 by about 3.5 nats; nets told the membership have L_own slightly negative (+0.4 nats at |r| = 3), and nets with fixed codes are in between (-1.3 to -1.6). The large-range departure of the A types follows the same order (0.088, 0.064, 0.018), a three-cohort pattern; within cohorts the types dominate. That this term is part of the standard nets' departure or cost is the hypothesis E64 tests by retraining with the codes outside block 1's LayerNorm.
- **Code geometry.** The per-source LayerNorm norm A varies by 13-15% through the random codes in the standard nets (0.65% in own, which do not need the codes in block 1), the routing leaks more when codes overlap, and idealising the codes at evaluation lowers every standard net's KL (14%).
- **For M2 (explain the inductive bias; predict from the architecture).** One property of pre-LN attention (a key's score depends on its error's size only through the norm and the sign) together with the routing requirement gives a single reading of three separate findings of this program: the two solution types (how the two heads are allocated), the larger sign dependence of B (one pooling head instead of an opposite-sign pair) and part of the departure (routing logits that lower large errors' scores). It predicts changes for retraining: removing the summaries option, taking the codes out of the normalisation, and supplying an even error feature (which E30's sign-free format did, with 11 of 12 A-type nets). These predictions are untested.
- **Limits.** Existing nets, one recipe and width; the 0.5 thresholds are registered, the "two pooling heads" criterion was found after the registered test; C is an attention-mass criterion, not a demonstrated consensus computation; L, dlogit and K_odd are algebraic parts of the logits (exact up to eps), not causal measurements, and dlogit at |r| = 3 is a reference value of one term; the ext nets share parents (11 clusters) and include hybrids and perturbed copies; fix also fixes the question codes and was trained on GPU; the code idealisation acts on trained nets at evaluation.

## Update 74 (2026-10-31 04:33Z): E65, across sizes the A/B types keep the two-pooling-head rule (P247) and every pooling head's routing logit has a negative norm term (P248); in the sign-free format A nets pool with one head and keep a consensus head (P249 fails); the width-128 norm term is weaker (P250) (amendment 73)

**TL;DR**
- **Design (CPU, existing nets).** E63's block-1 summary-head measures, unchanged, on E38's ctrl and mag nets at width 64, width 128 and depth 3 (10 seeds each) and on E37's 12 mag nets (width 32): 72 nets. In the mag format the o column carries |r|, so the linear coefficient (K_lin) multiplies an even feature, and the norm term is taken at |r| = +3. The decomposition is epsilon-free (relative denominator error at most 1.0e-4 over these 72 nets).
- **P247 holds.** A-type if and only if two pooling heads in 29 of 30 ctrl nets (w64 10 of 10, w128 10 of 10, d3 9 of 10; the exception, d3 s8, has rom_middle -0.002 and one pooling head). B nets have one pooling head or none (d3: 2 with none).
- **P248 holds.** All 37 pooling heads of the three ctrl cohorts have L_own > 0 (medians 14-19 by cohort and type) and a norm term dlogit(|r| = 3) < -1 (medians -2.9 to -3.6).
- **P249 fails on the allocation, holds on the linear coefficient.** In the mag format the A nets almost all have one pooling head (35 of 36 A nets; one w128 A net has none) and a consensus head in 35 of 36 (w32: 10 of 11), so "A iff two pooling heads" fails in every mag cohort (36 exceptions). All 36 mag pooling heads (35 in A nets, one in a B net) have a positive mean K_lin, a positive linear contribution to the score that grows with |r|, separate from the negative norm term; among the signed pooling heads the mean K_odd is positive in 33-62% by cohort.
- **P250 holds.** Median dlogit over the width-128 ctrl pooling heads -3.02, against -3.31 at width 32 (E63).
- **Post hoc (descriptive; A nets, four cohorts).** In the mag A nets the norm term weakens with size (median dlogit -3.06 at w32, -2.31 at d3, -2.02 at w64, -1.49 at w128) and their departures co-order (rom_large 0.063, 0.023, 0.016, -0.002). In the signed format the opposite-sign pairing of A's two pooling heads holds at every size (2 of 2, 4 of 4, 3 of 3).
- **What it shows.** The two-pooling-head rule for the signed format and the negative norm term of the routing logits are not width-32 artefacts: they hold over a fourfold width and an extra layer under this recipe. The sign-free format breaks the allocation rule: its A nets keep the consensus head that goes with B in the signed format and pool with one head whose linear coefficient on |r| is positive. So a consensus head does not by itself make a B net. A hypothesis compatible with E63 and E65, not demonstrated: in the signed format the linear part of a head's score favours one sign of the error, so pooling that treats both signs alike may need two heads with opposite signs (A), at the cost of the head that otherwise attends to the summaries; with |r| supplied, one head can favour large errors; this would fit E30 (the sign-free gain exceeds the measured sign cost), E37 (late removal of the signs rescues most B nets) and E39 (with |r| supplied the nets barely use the signs), whose heads were not measured here.
- **Review:** Codex (GPT-6) asked for five fixes, all done (`results/review_e65.md`):
  - necessity and mechanism were overclaimed (opposite mean coefficients do not show even pooling through unequal value and output maps, and E30, E37 and E39's heads were not measured): the sign-pair reading and its explanations are now a compatible hypothesis;
  - a positive K is not an increasing total score (the score change is L(A/n - 1) + K r A/n): reworded as a positive linear contribution beside the negative norm term;
  - counts: B nets have fewer than two pooling heads (two d3 nets have none), the mag A exceptions are listed (one w128 A net without a pooling head, one w32 A net without a consensus head), the 36 mag pooling heads include one B head, and the cohorts total 72 nets;
  - the size ordering concerns A nets of four cohorts, post hoc: "co-order", not "explain";
  - the epsilon-free approximation is now checked on these cohorts (at most 1.0e-4).
  It confirmed the head dimensions and the sqrt(d / dh) factor, block-1-only extraction, the mag encoding and the +3 term, acquisition, types and exclusions, the tables, P247, P248 and P250's passes and P249's failure.

**What this says.**
- **Across sizes (signed format).** A nets pool with two block-1 summary heads whose signed coefficients have opposite signs, B nets with fewer, mostly with a consensus head, at widths 32-128 and at depth 3 (29 of 30 here, 222 of 222 in E63). Every pooling head's routing logit has a negative norm term, slightly weaker at width 128 (P250), where the departure is about half; within each type the departures are also smaller at width 128 (A 0.027, B 0.088, against w32's 0.088, 0.159).
- **The sign-free format.** There the A nets pool with one head whose linear coefficient on |r| is positive and keep a consensus head. A consensus head does not by itself make a B net; what the types' allocation reflects in the signed format may be whether the pooling can treat both signs alike, which a single head's linear term cannot do with signed errors. That reading is a hypothesis compatible with E30, E37 and E39; E64's nocons arm, which removes the consensus option in the signed format, bears on it.
- **Post hoc: the norm term and the departure with size in the sign-free A nets.** The norm term weakens from -3.06 (w32) to -1.49 (w128) while the departure falls from 0.063 to -0.002, co-ordered over the four sizes; in the signed A nets the change is smaller (-3.55 to -2.95) and the departures fall too. These are associations across four cohorts.
- **For M2 (across sizes; predict from the architecture).** The head-level account (pre-LN scores depend on an error's size only through the norm and the linear term; routing makes the norm term negative; in the signed format A pairs opposite-sign heads, while with |r| supplied one head pools) now describes both formats, widths 32-128 and depth 3 under this recipe. It is a description with untested causal claims, and it does not yet give the departure's size.
- **Limits.** Existing nets, one recipe; 10 nets per E38 cohort (only 2 A nets at width 64); depth-3 types are close to the zero line; the mag norm term uses |r| = +3 only; K and dlogit are algebraic parts of block-1 logits, not weights or causal effects; the size co-ordering is post hoc over four cohorts.

## Update 75 (2026-10-31 05:18Z): E66, removing the signed term of a pooling head multiplies the KL by 4-17 (P256); in A nets a single removal raises the sign share to B's level (P257), in B nets less than twofold (P258); nets told the membership are less sensitive (P259) (amendment 74)

**TL;DR**
- **Design (CPU, existing nets; an evaluation-time surgery).** In block 1, for the summary rows of a chosen pooling head, the signed term of the labelled keys' logits is removed (logit_j minus q.W_K(gamma u~) r_j / (sigma_j sqrt(dh)), with LayerNorm's eps; key bias and LayerNorm beta stay in the key-independent constant), leaving the norm term, the values, every other row and head and block 2's operations unchanged (its activations change). Nets: E37's 10 ctrl and E30's 7 fix nets with at least one pooling head (E63's heads: 8 A nets with two, 9 B nets with one) and E60's 12 own nets. Conditions: base, each pooling head alone, all pooling heads. Per condition on E27's first 3,000 bases: KL, the sign-flip family's KL reduction (sign cost) and mean KL, their ratio (sign share); rom on the E12 pairs for base and all-removed.
- **P256 holds.** Removing the signed term from one pooling head multiplies the KL by 3.6-17 (medians 8.0 ctrl A, 12.1 ctrl B, 8.8 fix A, 8.5 fix B): 25 of 25 cases >= 3. The nets are very sensitive to this term.
- **P257 holds as registered.** In the 8 A nets a single removal raises the sign share from 0.05-0.09 to 0.39-0.54 (16 of 16 at least doubled; median ratio 6.5 ctrl, 6.0 fix); removing both gives 0.15-0.20, below the single removals in 8 of 8. But the absolute sign cost rises further with both removed (ctrl A means 0.0005, 0.031, 0.044 for base, single, both; fix A 0.0004, 0.021, 0.039) while the family KL rises faster (0.0074, 0.066, 0.25), so the smaller share does not show cancellation.

(base KL is on E27's 3,000 bases, not the registered test set; per-net values in `results/e66_tables.md`.)

**E66.2 Predictions**

| # | test | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| P256 | ctrl and fix: single removal multiplies KL by >= 3 in >= 80% of cases | holds: 25 of 25 |
| P257 | A nets: single removal at least doubles the sign share (>= 80%), both below single (>= 75% of nets) | holds: 16 of 16; 8 of 8 (the "both" result comes from the family KL's faster rise) |
| P258 | B nets: sign share ratio in [0.5, 2] in >= 75% | holds: 9 of 9 |
| P259 | own's median single-removal KL factor below ctrl's | holds: 7.3 against 10.2 |

**What this says.**
- **Sensitivity to the signed term.** A pooling head's weights depend on a labelled token's error through the LayerNorm norm (nearly even; the cross term 2 r a.u~ makes it slightly odd) and through the signed term. The nets' KL grows 4-17-fold when that term is removed from one head, more than for any other intervention in this lane, so the trained pooling relies on it heavily. Under softmax weights, a small signed coefficient beta shifts the weighted mean of z = r / n by about beta Var_w(z) beyond its base value, an even, roughly quadratic statistic of the errors, which is one way such a head can carry the reliability Bayes needs; each head's version depends on the signs at higher order.
- **A's two heads and the signs.** An A net's sign share is low only with both heads' terms in place; removing either brings it to about B's post-removal level. With E63's opposite-sign pairing this is compatible with the two heads cancelling each other's sign dependence, which would account for A's smaller sign dependence (E27: 7% against 25%); the test does not exclude other readings, since the value and output maps of the two heads differ and the full removal raises the absolute sign cost further.
- **The departure.** In the standard A nets, removing both signed terms raises the departure five- to sixfold, so those terms are needed to hold it down against the cap and the routing's negative norm term (E63). In B nets the single removal changes it little; in own nets the full removal breaks the nets (KL x38-55), so the near-zero departure there does not show what corrects it.
- **For M2 (why they deviate).** The standard nets' reliance on sign-dependent scores is consistent with how a pre-LN attention head can build an even statistic from signed tokens (through the signed term, under softmax normalisation), and A's lower sign dependence goes with having two such heads in opposite directions. Supplying |r| (E30, E65) or the membership (E60, E63) changes what the heads need; how much of the standard nets' sign dependence these mechanisms explain is not yet quantified.
- **Limits.** Evaluation-time surgery on trained nets, far off their operating point (KL factors measure sensitivity, not the training mechanism); 17 standard and 12 own nets; the sign share is a geometric-averaging measure; rom measured for base and full removal only; exact forward equality checked on plumbing nets only.

- **Post hoc (`e64b_post.py`, and a table extension): the content normaliser's cap scale.** With the codes out of it, the error feature's normaliser is the content part alone, and its cap scale is small: median c 0.56 (split; range 0.54-1.13) and 1.08 (splitnc; 0.54-1.15), against 3.8 in ctrl. This bundled intervention (it also fixes each token's code length and lowers the cap scale; the codes stay in the residual stream) is consistent with the head-level account's central claim (E63-E66), that the standard nets' main cost is the coupling, through the shared LayerNorm, of the routing score with how an error's size enters the score; matched ablations would be needed to attribute it. It does not reduce the departure or most of the code dependence; the failed predictions do not by themselves say where those come from. Barring the summaries head as well (splitnc) gives a higher KL.

**What this says.**
- **Consistent with the shared normaliser being the main cost.** With the routing codes normalised apart from the evidence, the nets still find a source's tokens by content (the code channel separates own from other keys by about 11 nats), yet their mean KL is similar to that of nets told the membership, and none is B-type. In the standard nets the same routing shares LayerNorm with the error feature, which goes with routing scores that lower large errors' scores (E63) and with pooling through the sign-dependent route and an opposite-sign pair (E66). With the coupling removed the norm contribution turns positive (median L_own -1.28, like own's -0.82), and most nets pool with a single head and keep the summaries head, as in the sign-free format (E65). This is a bundled intervention, so the attribution to the coupling as such is a hypothesis that it supports.
- **Suggestive non-additivity (reanalysis of E37 and E60).** Either change alone removes most of ctrl's excess KL: membership given with signed evidence (own, 0.0042) or content routing with sign-free evidence (mag, E37: mean 0.0055, median 0.0040; its one B net at 0.022); split adds a third way (0.0045). Independent additive costs would extrapolate to a negative KL for membership and sign-free inputs together (0.0042 + 0.0055 - 0.0127 = -0.0030), which is impossible; but a KL floor also breaks additive extrapolation, the fourth cell (membership given with sign-free inputs) was not trained, and the contrast has no interval, so this suggests, without establishing, that the excess needs content routing and signed evidence together.
- **What it does not remove.** The departure stays near ctrl's (0.12 against 0.13). Post hoc, separating the codes shrinks the error feature's cap scale to about 0.6 (the content part's norm has no code energy), so capping is stronger, and the learned weighting corrects about half of the cap's large-range departure and all of its middle-range one. The code dependence falls only from 28% to 13-16% (own 1.6%): the separately normalised code channel still carries code-dependent information into the scores and values.
- **Barring the summaries head.** With it barred (splitnc), 10 of 11 A nets pool with an opposite-sign pair and the mean KL is higher (0.0058 against 0.0045); that the consensus over the readings carries information Bayes uses (the query readings' marginal) is a hypothesis this fits.
- **For M2 (predict the cost from the architecture).** An architectural change derived from the head-level account, keeping routing codes out of the evidence's normalisation, was predicted to remove most of the standard nets' KL excess and to make them A-type, and did (P253, P255). Its predictions for the departure and the code dependence failed; the cap scale the change leaves (post hoc) and the code channel itself are candidates, not established causes.
- **Limits.** One recipe and width; 12 seeds per arm; split also normalises each token's code part to a fixed norm (it removes the random code length) and changes the cap scale, so the arm changes more than the coupling; GPU-trained, compared with GPU-trained ctrl and CPU-trained own (E60's device check); E64's codeln arm, which tested the coupling with a weak code channel, is reported separately.

That is compatible with two costs of content routing in the standard architecture: the head budget (changed here) and the routing-normaliser coupling (changed by E64b's split); both interventions are bundled, so the split into two costs is a reading, not an attribution.
- **For M2 (predict from the architecture).** Two architectural changes derived from the head-level account, each predicted before training, came out as the account said: more heads gave A-type nets with a 7.4% sign share (here), and a separate normalisation for the routing codes gave a mean KL similar to the membership-given nets' (E64b). Both are bundled interventions consistent with the account; the departure's size remains its open quantitative piece.
- **Limits.** One recipe, width and task; 12 seeds; the head dimension halves (8), which can change routing and pooling in other ways; the head roles are attention-mass criteria; the comparison is with E37's GPU-trained ctrl nets of the same seeds and initial values.

That each fix removes most, but not all, of a shared cost is a hypothesis these numbers are compatible with (the membership-given nets' sign share was 5.8%, E60).
- **The best learned pool.** Membership plus |r| reaches KL 0.0034 and a departure of 0.03, close to the exact-statistic uniform pool without LayerNorm (0.0032, departure 0 by construction): when neither routing nor sign dependence is in play, learned pooling with LayerNorm comes close to the floor set by reading an exact statistic.
- **For M2.** Under this recipe the standard architecture's three main deviations from the uniform-pool level can each be removed by an architectural or format change derived from the head-level account: the B type and its sign dependence by enough block-1 heads (E69, E70), most of the KL excess by separating the routing codes' normalisation (E64b) or by giving the membership (E60), and most of the remaining sign-related cost by sign-free inputs (E30, here). The departure's size is the remaining quantitative gap.
- **Limits.** One recipe and width; 12 seeds per arm; b1h4 also halves block 1's head width; ownmag trained on GPU, own on CPU (E60's device check covered four ctrl seeds, not the own architecture); the redundancy rule's 0.80 threshold was set before the data and the outcome is undecided, not a pass.

## Update 81 (2026-10-31 10:45Z): E64, barring block 1's summaries from each other gives 11 of 12 A-type nets with opposite-sign pairs (P242) and about half of ctrl's KL on paired seeds; the flawed codeln and both arms end B-type with about twice ctrl's KL (P243b-P246 fail) (amendment 72)

**TL;DR**
- **Design (CPU, retraining).** Three block-1 variants that keep content-based routing, 12 seeds each, every parameter starting as E37's ctrl net, same episodes, fixed 90,000-step schedule, on General's CPU: nocons (summary tokens barred from the other summaries), codeln (the code part of the embedding added after the content's LayerNorm, unnormalised), both (codeln and nocons). Addendum 1 to amendment 72 stated, after seeing the seed-0 runs' plateaus and before any other codeln or both result was analysed, that codeln's code channel starts about five times weaker than the baseline's, so that it would not test the coupling as intended; E64b's split arm was registered as the corrected test (itself a bundled change).
- **P242 holds.** 11 of 12 nocons nets (92%) have two pooling heads and are A-type; all 11 pairs have opposite-sign signed coefficients. The twelfth (seed 3) is B with no pooling head: one head on itself (self mass 0.97, which the consensus criterion counts) and one mostly on other sources' labelled tokens (0.69).
- **P245 fails.** Paired mean KL ratio nocons / ctrl 0.51 [0.37, 0.73] (11 seeds; holds), but codeln / ctrl 2.27 [1.56, 3.44] (9 seeds).
- **P243 fails.** (a) codeln's median pooling-head L_own 0.31 (bar 8.4; holds); (b) rom_large 1.32 [1.05, 1.64] of ctrl's (bar 0.7).
- **P244 fails.** both's KL is 6.05 [4.08, 9.06] of own's and its rom_large 0.170.
- **P246 fails.** Code share 0.523 [0.503, 0.543] (codeln) and 0.431 [0.371, 0.517] (both), against ctrl's 0.276 (bar 0.138).
- **Descriptive.** nocons: mean KL 0.0086 (median 0.0067; seed 3 at 0.032), rom_large 0.090 (0.64 of ctrl's), sign share 0.052, code share 0.307 [0.221, 0.389], c_seed(9) 0.46; its pooling heads keep a large positive norm-scaled logit (median 21.2; norm term -3.7 at |r| = 3). codeln: 2 stalls, 10 B; KL 0.0315; both: 12 B, KL 0.0255; their pooling-head counts are mixed (0-2) and the A-type pairing is rare (2 and 4 nets).
- **What it shows.** Removing block 1's option of attending to the other summaries leaves the summaries' self-attention and other sources' tokens available, and 11 of 12 nets then pool with an opposite-sign pair and end A-type, at about half of ctrl's KL on the paired seeds (0.51; 0.68 on all nets' means) and a quarter of its sign share: a third test (with E69 and E70) supporting the head-allocation reading, from the opposite direction (removing an option instead of adding heads). The unnormalised code channel (codeln, both) made routing slow to learn, consistent with the weakness stated before the full analysis, and those nets ended with higher KL, departures and code shares than ctrl (their sign shares were lower); neither they nor E64b's split isolates the coupling.
- **Review:** Codex (GPT-6) asked for five fixes, all done (`results/review_e64.md`):
  - the status synthesis paragraph turned approximations into mechanisms (the normaliser is nearly even with a cross term, the feature saturates, E66 showed sensitivity, the variance statistic is a candidate): reworded in the status;
  - nocons does not eliminate B or force pooling (only other summaries are barred; seed 3 is B with self-attention and attention to other sources' tokens): "11 of 12 become A", the surviving B allocation described, and the consensus criterion's inclusion of self-attention noted;
  - the codeln caveat was written after the seed-0 plateaus were seen, and E64b is also bundled: neither isolates the coupling; the failed predictions stand;
  - intervals copied from the saved JSON, and the 0.51 labelled as the 11-seed paired ratio (all-net means 0.68, medians 0.64);
  - the blanket "worse in every respect" contradicted the lower sign shares, and "does not touch" the code dependence was untested: the worsened metrics are named, and no demonstrated reduction is stated.
  It confirmed the architectures, the evaluators, the registered scoring (P242, P243a and nocons's part of P245 hold) and the tables.

| # | test | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| P242 | >= 80% of acquired nocons nets with two pooling heads and A-type | holds: 11 of 12 |
| P243 | codeln: (a) median L_own <= 0.5 x ctrl's; (b) rom_large <= 0.7 x ctrl's | (a) holds: 0.31; (b) fails: 1.32 |

| P246 | code shares of codeln and both <= 0.5 x ctrl's | fails: 0.523; 0.431 |

**What this says.**
- **The summaries option and the pair.** With block 1's summaries barred from the other summaries, 11 of 12 nets pool with both heads as an opposite-sign pair and become A-type, the KL falls (paired ratio 0.51; medians 0.0067 against ctrl's 0.0104) and the sign share falls to 5%. Together with E69 and E70 (more block-1 heads: all A, with both roles), this approaches the allocation from both sides: adding heads or removing the summaries option each makes nearly every net A-type in this recipe (E69 and E70 confound head count and width; here one net found another B allocation). The routing logits stay large (median 21.2) and the KL stays well above the membership-given nets' (2.05 [1.45, 3.13] of own's), compatible with the routing-normaliser coupling remaining. The nocons nets' code share (0.31) shows no reduction from ctrl's.
- **The flawed arms.** codeln and both put the code part of the embedding after the content's LayerNorm unnormalised, so it starts about five times weaker than in the baseline (stated in addendum 1 after the seed-0 plateaus were seen). Routing was then learned late or badly (two stalls, every acquired net B-type, KL about twice ctrl's, departures and code shares above ctrl's, sign shares below), which is consistent with the weak-channel explanation; the registered predictions for these arms failed and stand as failures. E64b's split, with both parts normalised, gave the predicted KL and types (Update 78) but also changes code length and the cap scale, so neither arm isolates the coupling.
- **For M2.** The head-allocation reading of the A/B types now has three supporting interventions in this recipe (E64 nocons, E69, E70), each predicted from the account and each bundled with other changes. That the B type's extra sign dependence comes from its single sign-dependent pooling head fits all three (sign shares 5-7% with the pair, 20% in ctrl).
- **Limits.** One recipe and width; 12 seeds per arm; CPU-trained arms against GPU-trained ctrl (E60's device check on four ctrl seeds); nocons changes only block 1's summary rows (block 2's summaries can still attend to each other); codeln and both are flawed, as stated in addendum 1 after the seed-0 plateaus were seen and before the full analysis.

## Update 82 (2026-10-31 16:44Z): E72, a factorised constrained-Bayes benchmark of block 1's own-source pool matches the A-type departure (P281, P282) as an offset of two opposite parts: at fixed summary-row attention A nets exceed it and B nets fall short (P290, P291), and the summary rows' query dependence lowers the departure (P289); the own-pool intervention removes the A departure (P286); P283, P284 and P287 fail (amendment 80, addendum 1)

**TL;DR**
- **Design (CPU, existing nets).** For 147 acquired nets of 13 held-out cohorts (E37 ctrl and mag, E30 fix, E60 own, E64 nocons, E69 h4, E70 b1h4 and ownmag, E38 at widths 64 and 128 in both formats; calibration E53 uni; E38 depth 3 descriptive), constrained-Bayes (CB) benchmarks of four reductions of block 1's own-source pool, read on E12's matched pairs: M0 (uniform capped feature at the net's cap scale), M1 (the reduced pooling model, three numbers per head), M2 (the real own-key attention with two pooled features) and M3 (the real pooled value vectors). Each is a classifier estimate of p(v | T) from simulated sources, combined over sources as if their statistics were independent given the variances (they share labels and question codes), with the derivative taken at fixed T. Part 2: single-route interventions on the summary's own pool (i), the query's block-1 read (ii) and block 2's read of the labelled tokens (iii). Addendum 1, registered after a dev-net finding and before any held-out CB result was opened: the rom with the summary rows' block-1 queries detached (detq), which keeps the forward unchanged and holds the summary rows' attention fixed in the derivative, as the benchmarks hold T fixed. Method developed on E43's newinit s0, s1, s2, s4 and s11 (dev nets, excluded).
- **P281 holds.** M3 is within 0.03 of the net's rom_large in 79 of 100 A nets (all of ctrl, w64ctrl, w128ctrl, w128mag, nocons; 11 of 12 own; 9 of 12 h4 and b1h4; none of the 4 fix A nets).
- **P282 holds.** M3's middle-range rom is negative (group A's sign) in 97 of 100 A nets.
- **P283 fails.** Over the 11 cohorts with at least three A nets, the rank correlation of cohort-mean M3 with cohort-mean rom_large is 0.54 (bar 0.6): fix A (M3 -0.015 against 0.064) and the sign-free cohorts (M3 above the nets) are off.
- **P284 fails.** M1 falls short of the net by more than 0.03 in 45 of 76 routing-A nets (59%): in nearly all signed-input A nets (ctrl 4 of 4, nocons 11 of 11, h4 and b1h4 11 of 12) but few sign-free ones (mag 2 of 11, w64mag 0 of 7, w128mag 0 of 9).
- **P285 holds.** M3 is at least 1.5 times the net's rom_large in 19 of 23 B nets with a pooling head (ctrl 6 of 6, w128ctrl 6 of 6, w64ctrl 6 of 8, fix 1 of 3); 11 B nets have no pooling head.
- **P286 holds.** In 64 of 66 A nets of the standard-forward cohorts, the own-pool intervention (i) changes the big-miss weight by the net's rom within 0.03, and the intervention on block 2's read (iii) by at most 0.02.
- **P287 fails.** The B pattern (c_i at least 1.3 times the net's rom, c_iii negative) holds in 17 of 33 B nets: 17 of 21 with the usual inputs (ctrl, w64ctrl, w128ctrl), 0 of 8 fix B nets (c_i 0.07 of a 0.20 departure) and 0 of 4 sign-free B nets (extreme single-route values, c_i near -3).
- **P288 holds.** In all 12 uniform-pool nets M3 is within 0.03 (mean 0.155 against 0.172).
- **P289 holds.** Detaching the summary rows' block-1 queries raises rom_large in 126 of 135 nets, with identical predictions.
- **P290 holds.** At fixed summary-row attention, M3 is below the net's rom by more than 0.02 in 87 of 100 A nets.
- **P291 holds.** At fixed summary-row attention, M3 exceeds the net's rom by more than 0.05 in 20 of 23 B nets (ctrl B: 0.44 against 0.21).
- **What it shows.** Per net the departure is the sum of three measured quantities: M3, the departure of a factorised benchmark that reads only the source's own pool; detq - M3, the net's departure at fixed summary-row attention beyond that benchmark (this includes the net's reading and every route other than the own pool's query dependence); and rom - detq, the effect of the summary rows' query dependence (the source's reading is part of its summary's query). In A nets the second is +0.02 to +0.07 by cohort and the third -0.015 to -0.05 (fix A +0.011), so they largely cancel and the total stays close to M3; P281's agreement is this offset, not the benchmark describing the net's reading. M3's cohort means vary two to three times as much as either other part (about 0 with membership given, 0.065-0.08 in the content-routing cohorts at width 32, 0.02 at width 128) and carry group A's middle-range sign, but they order the cohorts' departures only moderately (P283 fails). In B nets with a pooling head the benchmark's departure is about three times the net's and the net at fixed attention stays far below it. The reduced model with three numbers per head falls short in the signed format only.
- **Review:** Codex (GPT-6, `gpt-6-astra`) asked for five fixes, all done (`results/review_e72.md`):
  - (high) the nocons nets were loaded without their mask (the shared loader never reaches `pfn_e64`): fixed in `pfn_l2fix.py`, and nocons's Part 1 and addendum recomputed; no registered count changed, and the recomputed rom now matches the registered one in every net;
  - (high) "ideal reasoner" and "information loss" overstated the estimator (a classifier-based benchmark, factorised over sources that share labels and question codes, with the statistic held fixed): reworded throughout as a factorised constrained-Bayes benchmark;
  - (high) detq does not isolate a pure reader term (it detaches the summary rows' queries in every head, and other routes stay live): the three parts are now described operationally;
  - (medium) the route results are single-route interventions, not mediation, and do not locate the fixed-code B nets' remainder: reworded;
  - (medium) mixed denominators (fix B): every column of E72.1 now uses the same matched nets.
  It confirmed the stored verdicts against `results/e72.json`, the thresholds, exclusions and B filter as registered, and the disclosure of the dev-tuned thresholds and of the addendum's timing.
- **Decision for Kelvin:** none.

**E72.3 Predictions**

| # | test | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| P281 | \|M3 - net\| <= 0.03 in >= 75% of A | holds: 79 of 100 |
| P282 | M3 rom_middle < 0 in >= 75% of A | holds: 97 of 100 |
| P283 | cohort-mean Spearman >= 0.6 (>= 8 cohorts) | fails: 0.54 over 11 cohorts |
| P284 | M1 < net - 0.03 in >= 75% of routing-A | fails: 45 of 76 |
| P285 | M3 >= 1.5 x net in >= 75% of B | holds: 19 of 23 |
| P286 | \|c_i - net\| <= 0.03 and \|c_iii\| <= 0.02 in >= 75% of A (Part 2) | holds: 64 of 66 |
| P287 | c_i >= 1.3 x net and c_iii < 0 in >= 75% of B (Part 2) | fails: 17 of 33 |
| P288 | \|M3 - net\| <= 0.03 in >= 75% of uni | holds: 12 of 12 |
| P289 | detq - base > 0 in >= 75% of nets (addendum) | holds: 126 of 135 |
| P290 | M3 < detq - 0.02 in >= 75% of A (addendum) | holds: 87 of 100 |
| P291 | M3 > detq + 0.05 in >= 75% of B (addendum) | holds: 20 of 23 |

**What this says.**
- **Where the departure is made, by intervention.** In A nets, letting only the source's own block-1 pool see the spread version of its errors removes about the whole departure (P286, 64 of 66; E25's site in an older cohort), and the same intervention on the query's block-1 read or on block 2's direct read changes it by at most about 0.02. These are single-route interventions against detach-only controls, not an additive mediation analysis; in the wide A nets the detach-only effect of route (iii) itself is large (median +0.32 at width 128), which the controls absorb.
- **Three parts of different sign.** At fixed summary-row attention the A nets show a larger departure than the benchmark of their own pool (P290), and the summary rows' query dependence lowers the departure (P289). Both parts are similar across very different A cohorts (membership given or not, two or four heads, barred summaries, widths, formats; cohort means +0.019 to +0.068 and -0.050 to -0.015, with fix A's +0.011 the exception) and largely cancel. The second part is an operational difference: it contains the net's reading of its pool and every other route, and the benchmark itself is approximate (factorised over sources, classifier-estimated, PCA at width 64-128), so it is not a pure reader term. M3 varies more between cohorts: about 0 when membership is given (own and ownmag: their departure, 0.018 and 0.029, is then the other two parts), 0.065-0.08 in the content-routing cohorts at width 32, 0.02 at width 128; its cohort means order the departures only moderately (P283: 0.54), with fix A (M3 -0.015 against 0.064) and the sign-free cohorts (M3 above the nets) off.
- **B nets.** Where they have a pooling head, the benchmark of that head's pool shows about three times the net's departure (P285), and at fixed summary-row attention the nets stay far below it (P291; ctrl B: detq 0.21 against M3 0.44); in the usual format the intervention on block 2's read lowers the weight's departure (17 of 21). Eleven B nets have no pooling head at all (1 ctrl, 5 fix, 1 nocons, 4 sign-free), and in the fixed-code B nets the own-pool intervention removes only about a third of the departure; "B" covers more than one mechanism.
- **The reduced model.** Three numbers per head (mean routing logit, signed coefficient, cap scale) fall short of the departure in the signed-input cohorts but not in the sign-free ones (P284 fails overall). On the dev nets the shortfall came from the source-to-source variation of the pooling coefficients (a ladder with source-specific coefficients recovered the real pool's CB value), which idealised codes do not remove and which the downstream compensates (a dev-net surgery; addendum 1). This was not tested on held-out nets.
- **For M2 (predict the departure from the architecture).** For A nets the departure now has a measured three-part decomposition across 12 cohorts, in which the part that varies most between architectures is what the source's own pool preserves (as judged by a factorised benchmark) and the other two parts, of opposite sign, are similar across architectures. What sets each part, and why the second and third are so similar across architectures, is not derived here; that is needed before the departure is predicted from the architecture.
- **Limits.** Classifier estimates (about 0.001 on known cases); M3's value vectors include code and label parts; the factorised benchmark ignores shared labels and question codes; the derivative conventions differ between the benchmark (fixed T) and the net (the addendum aligns one route only); the cohorts share seeds and initial values; the models and thresholds were chosen on five dev nets of one cohort; two loader errors were found and fixed after the first analysis; the fixed-code, sign-free B and depth-3 nets are not explained.

- **What it shows.** Under this recipe, across the five tested block-1 layouts, the type tracks the number of block-1 heads rather than their width: two heads give mostly B at either width (4 of 11, 2 of 11), four give mostly or only A at either width (11 of 12, 12 of 12), and the KL differences go with the count (a factor of two to two and a half), while the width contrasts have intervals that cover zero (at two heads [-0.23, +0.70] on the log scale, compatible with a moderate effect). The total attention dimension, the parameter count, the output map's initial scale and the device change with the layouts, so this supports the head-count account without proving the head budget the unique cause. Three heads, the number the account says the three jobs need, are mostly but not always enough (9 of 12) and lower the sign share less than predicted (P278's failure); in two of their B nets the third head meets neither criterion and looks mostly at other sources' labelled tokens. Two-head nets can still be A, so three heads are not necessary. The registered prediction that spare heads pair by 5,000 steps failed (pooled median 10,000; h4w16 5,000, post hoc), which does not exclude a competition effect on the timing.

**What this says.**
- **Head count rather than head width.** At either head dimension, two block-1 heads give mostly B nets (ctrl 4 of 11 A, h2w8 2 of 11) and four give A nets (h4w16 11 of 12, b1h4 12 of 12); the paired log-KL contrasts for the count are -0.69 (dimension 16) and -0.93 (dimension 8), those for the dimension +0.21 and +0.06 with intervals covering zero. So the confound left by E69 and E70 resolves toward the count: the evidence supports the number of block-1 attention patterns as the factor, and halving the head dimension (with it the rank of each head's query-key map for the 16-dimensional codes) did not make A or change the KL detectably in this range, although the two-head width interval does not exclude a moderate effect and the other quantities that change with the layouts are not separated.
- **The threshold.** Three heads, one per job in the account (a summaries head and an opposite-sign pooling pair), give 9 of 12 A nets, 10 of 12 with the predicted roles, a KL between the two- and four-head cells (0.0078 against 0.0127 and 0.0056) and a sign share between them (0.135 against 0.200 and 0.099). In two of the three B nets the third head meets neither criterion (it puts 0.77 and 0.76 of its mass on other sources' labelled tokens, the pattern of nocons s3 in E64 and of several fixed-code B nets in E63), and one four-head net puts two heads on the summaries and one on pooling: a sufficient head budget makes the A allocation likely, not certain, so which allocation a net reaches is also a matter of training (as E43-E47 found for the two-head nets' initial values). Attention mass does not establish what these heads compute.
- **Timing.** With spare heads, the pair is first seen at a median of 10,000 steps, as in the two-head A lineages (E68), and every first pair has opposite signs; the four heads of dimension 16 pair somewhat earlier (median 5,000, post hoc). The registered prediction that spare heads pair by 5,000 steps fails; equal pooled medians do not exclude some competition effect, and what sets the pair's timing is open.
- **For M2 (predict from the architecture).** Across five block-1 layouts (two, three and four heads; dimensions 8 and 16) the head count predicted the type mix: mostly B with two heads, mostly A from three, with the KL following the count and the sign dependence only partly (three heads above the registered bar). The prediction is a likelihood, not a rule (9 of 12 at three heads), and it was tested at width 32 with block 2 fixed at two heads.
- **Limits.** One recipe and width; the total attention dimension and the parameter count change with the cells (h2w8 16 dimensions and 16,636 parameters; h3w16 48; h4w16 64 and 22,924; ctrl and b1h4 32 and 18,732); E71 trained on CPU, ctrl and b1h4 on GPU; pooling and consensus are attention-mass criteria; the trajectory checkpoints are sparse (a pair formed between checkpoints is dated at the next one).

| # | test | outcome |

| P292 | A: M3(5k) - M3(90k) >= 0.6 x (rom(5k) - rom(90k)) in >= 3 of 4 | holds: 4 of 4 |

| secondary | P292 and P296 each in >= 75% of the h4 and of the b1h4 lineages | fails: P292 11 of 12 and 12 of 12; P296 2 of 12 and 6 of 12 |

**What this says.**
- **Two kinds of trajectory.** In A lineages M3, the departure a factorised benchmark reader of the source's own pool would show, falls with the rom in all four (P292); with the head set fixed from the opposite-sign pair's first appearance, it falls about threefold, in step with the rom, so in A lineages the later decay goes with what the pool preserves about a big miss. In B lineages M3 stays at about 0.44 (P293) and the net at fixed summary-row attention moves 0.12-0.20 further below it (P294); since that difference contains every route other than the own pool's query dependence and the benchmark's error, B's growing block-2 read of the labelled tokens (E34, E35) is a candidate, not an identified route. With both heads counted, B pools might also look less lossy, as A's did before their pair (not measured).
- **The other two parts.** The query-dependence term (rom - detq) has a median near zero at 5k and about -0.05 at 90k (P295; exceptions s0 and s8, and s0 is already -0.073 at 5k), and the A nets' excess at fixed attention has a median near zero at 10k and about +0.05 at 90k, with s1 negative at 10k (P296 fails as registered).
- **For M2 (how they learn; why they deviate).** Over training, the two types' departures shrink along different measured trajectories: in A lineages with the benchmark of the paired pool, in B lineages against a flat benchmark of the single pool. This fits the head-allocation account (the A allocation is the one whose pool keeps improving), but the decomposition is operational, and which part causes the B nets' decay, or what sets either type's final departure, is not identified here.
- **Limits.** The benchmark's limits (E72's review: factorised, classifier-estimated, statistic held fixed) and its dependence on which heads count as pooling heads (shown post hoc above); 4 A and 6 measurable B lineages in the primary set, all sharing E37's seeds; sparse checkpoints (a pair is dated at the next checkpoint); the fixed-head-set check covers only the two checkpoints around each A pair.

## Update 85 (2026-10-31 20:55Z): E75, shuffling a source's reading in its pooling heads' block-1 queries multiplies the B nets' test-NLL gap by 1.5 or more (P302) and barely changes most A nets' (P303), while raising the A departure (P305); the consensus heads' queries matter in more B nets than predicted (P304 fails) and the coefficient's correlation with the reading has a cohort-dependent sign (P306 fails) (amendment 83)

**TL;DR**
- **Design (CPU, existing nets; evaluation-time intervention).** In block 1, only the summary rows' queries of a chosen head set are recomputed from an input in which the source's reading is replaced by the same source's reading in another episode (a fixed derangement); keys, values, residuals and later blocks use the real input. Head sets: the pooling heads (P_h >= 0.5) and the consensus heads (C_h >= 0.5). Nets with pfn2's standard forward: ctrl, fix, h4, b1h4, mag and E38's four width cohorts (99 acquired nets: 66 A, 33 B; eligible sets A 38, Bp 23, Bc 27); E38's depth-3 cohorts descriptive; E71's arms secondary. The derangement cycles within evaluation batches (2,000 test rows, 1,000 pair rows). Measures: the test-NLL gap (an estimate of the KL) as a ratio to base, rom, and per pooling head the correlation of the source-mean signed coefficient K with the reading. Developed on E43's newinit s0, s1, s2, s4, s11 (dev, excluded).
- **P302 holds.** In 20 of 23 B nets with a pooling head the test-NLL gap rises at least 1.5-fold under shuf_pool (ctrl B: median 2.56 [1.78, 2.87]; fix B 4.40; w64ctrl B 2.44; w128ctrl B 2.43).
- **P303 holds.** In 31 of 38 A nets with two pooling heads the test-NLL gap rises at most 1.15-fold (ctrl A 1.07, h4 1.06, b1h4 1.03); the seven exceptions are three fix A nets (3.4-5.2) and four wide A nets (w64ctrl, w128ctrl medians 1.27, 1.28).
- **P304 fails.** The consensus heads' shuf_cons raises the test-NLL gap at most 1.10-fold in 16 of 27 B nets (bar 75%): ctrl B median 1.03 (but s5 1.51), fix B 1.40.
- **P305 holds.** shuf_pool raises the A nets' rom_large by at least 0.02 in 30 of 38 (ctrl A 0.088 to 0.121, h4 0.079 to 0.106, b1h4 0.085 to 0.111). The donor queries are constants in the derivative, so this combines a changed operating point with the removal of E72's derivative path; it is consistent with, not independent of, E72's result.
- **P306 fails (narrowly).** corr(K, o*) <= -0.20 for 17 of 23 B pooling heads (74%, bar 75%): the ctrl family's are negative (ctrl B median -0.30, w64ctrl -0.44, w128ctrl -0.55), fix B's positive (+0.33 to +0.67); |corr| <= 0.15 for 61 of 76 A pooling heads (80%).
- **Secondary (E71's arms).** P302 10 of 12 (h2w8 B median 2.07), P303 21 of 22, P305 21 of 22; P304 9 of 13 and P306's B part 8 of 13 fail as in the registered cohorts.
- **What it shows.** The B nets' performance depends on their single pooling head's summary-row query being consistent with the source's own reading: with another episode's reading there, the test-NLL gap rises about 2.5-fold in the usual nets, while on the dev nets the attention itself barely moved (total variation 0.015; not measured on the held-out nets). Most A nets' opposite-sign pairs depend on it little (31 of 38), although removing it raises their departure. The intervention shows dependence on a consistent query; whether the downstream uses reading-dependent information or is disturbed by a mismatched query is not separated. With fixed codes both types depend on it strongly, the wide A nets moderately, and the consensus head's query matters in some B nets.
- **Review:** Codex (GPT-6, `gpt-6-astra`) asked for five fixes, all done (`results/review_e75.md`):
  - (high) "the downstream relies on it" and the explanation of B's distance from E72's benchmark went beyond an intervention that shows dependence on a consistent query: reworded, with the benchmark link as a hypothesis, in both versions;
  - (medium) the acquired registered nets are 99 (66 A, 33 B), not 101, and P303's seven exceptions are three fix and four wide nets, not "mostly fix": corrected, with the eligible denominators;
  - (medium) "KL" is a sampled test-NLL gap: relabelled;
  - (medium) P305 also removes E72's derivative path, and "attention barely changed" is a dev-net observation: both stated where interpreted;
  - (low) the derangement cycles within batches: documented.
  It confirmed the selected-head isolation, the own-format tokens, the head classification, the forward's equality with the nets' own when nothing is replaced, the recomputed base values, P302-P306's scoring and every table value.
- **Decision for Kelvin:** none.

**E75.2 Predictions**

| # | test | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| P302 | Bp: gap(shuf_pool) / gap(base) >= 1.5 in >= 75% | holds: 20 of 23 |
| P303 | A: gap(shuf_pool) / gap(base) <= 1.15 in >= 75% | holds: 31 of 38 |
| P304 | Bc: gap(shuf_cons) / gap(base) <= 1.10 in >= 75% | fails: 16 of 27 |
| P305 | A: rom_large(shuf_pool) - rom_large(base) >= 0.02 in >= 75% | holds: 30 of 38 |
| P306 | corr(K, o*) <= -0.20 for >= 75% of Bp pooling heads and \|corr\| <= 0.15 for >= 75% of A pooling heads | fails: B 17 of 23 (74%); A 61 of 76 |

**What this says.**
- **A type-specific dependence on the reading inside the pool.** In the standard-code nets, keeping the B type's single pooling head's query consistent with the source's own reading matters for its test-NLL gap (about 2.5-fold when broken), and the A type's opposite-sign pair matters much less (31 of 38 within 15%). That B's reader uses a small, reading-dependent part of the pooled values, which a fixed-statistic benchmark like E72's cannot see and which would fit B's distance from that benchmark (E72, E73), is a hypothesis: the intervention cannot distinguish used information from disturbance by a mismatched query, and E72's benchmark does not exclude reading-dependent information in T. What such a part would compute (for example a product of the reading with a variance-like statistic) is untested.
- **Where it is and is not.** The consensus head's query matters little in most usual-format B nets but clearly in some (ctrl s5 1.51) and in the fixed-code B nets (1.40); with fixed codes, A nets also depend on the pooling heads' reading (3.4-5.2 in three of four), and the coefficient's correlation with the reading turns positive. The wide A nets (widths 64, 128) depend on it moderately (1.27-1.28).
- **The departure.** In A nets the intervention raises the departure (P305), in the direction of E72's derivative result; since it also removes that derivative path, it is not an independent forward-only confirmation.
- **For M2 (how transformers approximate Bayes; why the types differ).** Besides the head allocation and the pool's information about a big miss (E63-E73), the two types differ in how much their performance depends on a token's own content in its pooling query: the B type's single pooling head's query must stay consistent with the current reading, the A type's paired heads' much less. If that dependence is used information, it is one concrete way in which B departs from a pool-then-read Bayes reader; that remains to be shown.
- **Limits.** An evaluation-time intervention off the trained operating point (the shuffled reading is real data but mismatched to the episode); the attention change is small, so the downstream's use is inferred from the KL, not traced; standard-forward nets only (not own, nocons, uni); the fixed-code cohort and the wide cohorts differ from the ctrl family in sign and size.

## Update 86 (2026-11-01 16:46Z): E74, with six sources the content-routing nets' pooling heads have larger routing logits (P298) and the big-miss departure grows about 1.6- to 1.9-fold (P300) while membership-given nets keep a small one (P301); the growth of the KL ratio of content routing to membership given fails its registered criterion (P297), and the mean leakage growth (P299) comes from two late nets (amendment 82)

**TL;DR**
- **Design (CPU, retraining).** World 1 with S = 6 sources (`world_n.py`), pfn2's baseline at width 32 with two heads, train_n's fixed 90,000-step schedule, seeds 0-11: ctrl (content routing; summary rows find their source's labelled tokens by the random codes) and own (E60's restricted learned pool; membership given). Each seed starts from the same initial values as the three-source ctrl net of that seed; the episode stream is seeded by the config name with '_S6'. References at S = 3: E37's 11 acquired ctrl nets and E60's 12 own nets, re-evaluated with the same code on S = 3 data of the same construction (`e74_data.py`: 16,000 test episodes with exact Bayes NLL, E12-style matched pairs). Measures (`e74_eval.py`): the test-NLL gap (an estimate of the KL), rom_large and rom_middle, the type, and for ctrl block 1's summary-head measures (pooling and consensus heads, an opposite-sign pair, the norm-scaled own logit L_own and the norm term at |r| = 3 from E63's pre-LN decomposition, and leak = the pooling heads' mass on other sources' labelled tokens).
- **P297 fails its registered criterion.** Over the 10 seeds acquired in all four cells, (ctrl / own at S = 6) / (ctrl / own at S = 3) of the paired-mean KLs is 1.46 [0.98, 1.84] (bar: point >= 1.25 and lower limit >= 1.0; the bootstrap resamples seeds on fixed test episodes). R6 = 4.17 [2.21, 7.06], R3 = 2.86 [1.93, 4.30].
- **P298 holds.** The median L_own of ctrl's pooling heads is 25.3 at S = 6 against 16.8 at S = 3 (B 23.1 against 15.2, A 25.7 against 19.9); the median norm term at |r| = 3 is -4.71 against -3.31.
- **P299 holds on the registered mean.** The pooling heads' mean leak is 0.050 at S = 6 (11 nets) against 0.016 at S = 3 (10 nets; E37 s8 has no pooling head and is excluded, as registered). The medians are 0.019 and 0.018 (B nets with a pooling head: 0.0196 at both S); the mean comes from s8 (0.288) and s9 (0.099), the two nets that crossed the validation threshold last.
- **P300 holds.** ctrl's mean rom_large is 0.274 at S = 6 against 0.126; by type, B (with a pooling head) 0.289 (median; 0.267-0.448, 9 nets) against 0.151 (0.129-0.158, 6 nets), about 1.9-fold; A 0.126 and 0.129 against 0.069-0.084 (4 nets), about 1.6-fold.
- **P301 holds.** own's mean |rom_large| at S = 6 is 0.034 (S = 3: 0.015).
- **Post hoc, descriptive.** The paired KL statistic leans on s8 and s9 (S = 6 ctrl gaps 0.095 and 0.044, against 0.040 and 0.013 at S = 3): the ratio of medians is 1.02 and the paired per-seed log ratio has median +0.17 (positive in 6 of 10); without s8 and s9, a selection made after seeing them, the registered statistic is 1.06 [0.88, 1.30] (8 seeds). First validation check with gap < 0.10 (stored curves, every 1,000 steps; one threshold across S, not a calibrated acquisition point): ctrl at S = 6 at a median of 8,000 steps (6,000-14,000) in 9 nets, s9 at 66,000, s8 at 81,000, s4 never (test gap 0.18); ctrl at S = 3 at 4,000 (3,000-7,000), E37 s3 never; own at 1,000-2,000 at both S. The head-allocation rule holds in all 11 acquired S = 6 ctrl nets: the 2 A nets have two pooling heads with opposite-sign coefficients and no consensus head, the 9 B nets one pooling head and one consensus head. With the same initial values (but different episode streams), 4 of the 10 paired seeds change type between S = 3 and S = 6 (s0, s2, s6 A to B; s5 B to A).
- **What it shows.** Outside S = 3 the account's routing quantities and the departure moved together with the number of competing sources in the predicted direction: larger routing logits, a more negative norm term, a departure about 1.6-fold (A) and 1.9-fold (B) larger, and a small departure with membership given. The predicted growth of the KL cost of content routing relative to membership given failed its registered criterion; the data are compatible with anything from no growth to 84% growth, and the point estimate leans on two nets that crossed the validation threshold late. Content routing at S = 6 crossed that threshold later, ended B more often, and in typical B nets kept the same total leak spread over 2.5 times as many competing tokens.

| P301 | own's mean \|rom_large\| at S = 6 <= 0.05 | holds: 0.034 |

**What this says.**
- **The departure grew with the number of sources, together with the routing quantities.** With six sources each summary row must find its 4 labelled tokens among 20 other sources' labelled tokens and 6 summaries (against 8 and 3). Its pooling heads' norm-scaled own logit is larger (median 25 against 17, in both types), the norm term that lowers a large error's score is more negative (-4.7 against -3.3 at |r| = 3), and the departure is larger in both types (about 1.9-fold in B, 0.29 against 0.15; about 1.6-fold in the two A nets, 0.13 against 0.08), while nets told the membership keep a small one (0.034; 0.015 at S = 3). This co-movement is in the direction the routing account (E60-E64b, E72) predicts from the routing logit's norm term; L_own is not an isolated code contribution and the norm term is not the whole score, so the link is a hypothesis this test supports without isolating. The S = 6 decomposition of E72 (how much of the larger departure is the own pool's benchmark M3) was not measured.
- **The KL cost of routing: the registered growth test failed.** The paired statistic is 1.46 with an interval from 0.98 to 1.84; the ratio of medians is 1.02, the per-seed log ratios are positive in 6 of 10, and the two nets that crossed the threshold last carry much of the mean. The data neither show the predicted growth nor exclude a moderate one (without s8 and s9, chosen after seeing them, 1.06 [0.88, 1.30]).
- **Leak.** The B nets with a pooling head put 0.0196 of their pooling head's mass on other sources' labelled tokens at both S, although those tokens are 2.5 times as many, so the average mass per competing token is about 2.5 times lower; that this reflects sharper code discrimination is a hypothesis. P299's mean growth comes from s8 and s9 (0.29 and 0.10), which crossed the validation threshold at 81,000 and 66,000 steps and have the largest L_own (94 and 63). E37 s8, a B net without a pooling head, is outside P299's set; its head 0 puts 0.58 of its mass on other sources' labelled tokens (the third B kind noted in E63 and E71).
- **Timing and type.** Content routing at S = 6 crossed the validation threshold later (median 8,000 against 4,000 steps; the same gap threshold against a sharper Bayes), with one stall in each ctrl cohort and two late nets at S = 6, and the type mix moved toward B (2 of 11 A against 4 of 11). The head-allocation rule recurs in all 11 acquired nets. With the same initial values 4 of 10 seeds changed type; because the episode streams also differ, this is descriptive (under a new episode stream at S = 3, E43 found the type kept in 10 of 11).
- **For M2 (holds across tasks; predicts the departure from the architecture).** The first test of the account outside three sources supports its departure side as co-movement: the routing logit, its norm term and the departure grow together with the number of competing sources, and membership given keeps the departure small. The cost side failed its registered test and remains open: the KL excess of content routing may or may not grow with the number of sources in this range.
- **Limits.** One width and recipe; the S = 3 references were trained on GPU (E37) and CPU (E60) and the S = 6 nets on CPU (E60 found CPU and GPU agree on KL and rom); the episode streams differ between S; Bayes is sharper at S = 6, so KLs are compared as ratios; 10 paired seeds, 2 A nets at S = 6; the late nets dominate the means; leak and L_own are attention-based measures; the threshold crossing is not calibrated across S; the bootstrap is conditional on the fixed test episodes.

- **What it shows.** Under this recipe a reader trained from scratch on a trained net's frozen embedding and block 1 approximately reproduces the source's measured test-NLL gap (B within 4% on either weight choice; A within 14% on the end-of-schedule weights but 1.34-1.38 for two of four on the registered ones), and the trained reader's further training gains a median of about 5% (selected checkpoints) or 7% (after 90,000 steps). **What this says.**
- **The measured gap is approximately reproduced on a frozen block 1.** A reader trained from random values on a frozen embedding and block 1, with the original schedule and a new episode stream, ends near the source's test-NLL gap: within 4% in all six B nets on either weight choice; in the A nets within 14% on the end-of-schedule weights, but 1.34 and 1.38 times the source for s0 and s2 on the registered ones. Continuing the trained reader lowers the gap by a median of about 5% at the selected checkpoints and about 7% after the full 90,000 steps (4-18%). Under this recipe the remaining gap (0.006-0.016 nats here) therefore depends mostly on the frozen parts; that it is a limit of block 1's representation rather than an optimisation limit shared by readers trained this way is a hypothesis, and whether block 1 itself would improve with more training is not tested here.
- **A nets: the departure and its parts are reproduced.** The fresh reader reproduces rom_large, detq and the query term within 0.006, so in this recipe A's excess at fixed summary-row attention over E72's benchmark (+0.04 to +0.06 in the sources) is what a reader trained this way makes of these block-1 representations. The decomposition is operational (E72): detq includes every route other than the summary rows' query dependence.
- **B nets: a descriptive shift in the departure.** The query term is reproduced within 0.004, but the fresh readers' departure is lower by 0.009-0.026 in five of six (detq moves with it; s4 +0.002), at similar measured test-NLL gaps (sampled, without an uncertainty estimate). Continued training moves B's departure in the same direction, by less (median -0.007). So, at about the same measured gap, B readers trained on the same block 1 can differ in the departure by about 0.02; one fresh reader per source does not show how much of this is reader-seed variation.
- **For M2 (why they cannot learn better; how they learn).** With E69-E71 (more block-1 heads give A and about half the KL), these results point to block 1's allocation and representation, not the reader, as where the two-head nets' remaining distance from Bayes is set under this recipe: a candidate answer to why they do not learn better, to be tested by training block 1 further and by more readers per source.
- **Limits.** One recipe and width; the embedding and block 1 frozen, so the joint optimum is not tested; one fresh reader per source; the registered (validation-selected) and end-of-schedule weights differ by up to 0.0023 in gap for three A fresh readers; the continued reader's learning rate is one choice; test-NLL gaps without uncertainty estimates; 10 sources sharing E37's seeds; the decomposition's limits (E72's review) apply.

- **P312 holds (final weights only).** The median gap of the B sources' fresh2 readers is 0.0081, 1.80 times the A sources' 0.0045 (sources: 0.0126 and 0.0064, 1.98 times). On the best-validation weights the ratio is 1.29 (A median 0.0063), below the bar.
- **P313 holds.** In all 4 A sources rom_large(fresh2) is within 0.02 of the source's (-0.006 to -0.014).
- **P314 holds.** rom_middle(fresh2) keeps the source's sign in 10 of 10; the B sources' middle-range rom shrinks (median -0.027, to +0.028 to +0.050).
- **Descriptive.** B's departure falls with the second reader block: -0.025 to -0.047 against the source (median -0.032) and -0.007 to -0.036 against fresh1; the query term changes by at most 0.007. In every B source one head of the first reader block puts 0.33-0.55 of the summary rows' attention on their own labelled-token positions (the sources' block 2: 0.19-0.24), compatible with gathering them again at the summary rows (attention masses, not value content or causal contribution; a hypothesis); in the A sources this mass stays at 0.21-0.27, and their second reader block's query puts more of its mass on the labelled tokens (its larger head 0.43-0.70, against 0.09-0.40 in the sources' block 2). Joint depth 3 by its own type: A median gap 0.0040 (4 nets, 0.0036-0.0043), B 0.0097 (6 nets, 0.0027-0.0269); paired by seed (8 seeds, with type changes) joint3 / source has median 0.62 and fresh2 / source 0.70, and the departure falls more in joint3 (median -0.051 against -0.020). The two joint3 nets with a block-2 head whose summary rows put all their attention on their own labelled tokens (s7, s8: 1.00 rounded) have two of the three lowest gaps (0.0027, 0.0038; s9 0.0036) (post hoc).
- **What it shows.** Under this recipe E76's one-block readers were part of what limits the nets: a second reader block on the same frozen block 1 lowers the gap by about a third in every source, in both types, to distances comparable by type with E38's jointly trained depth-3 nets (a comparison confounded by training budget, device, episodes and the nets' own types). A source-associated A/B difference persists with the deeper reader (1.8 times on the registered weights, 1.3 on the best-validation ones); one reader fit per source cannot separate a representation limit of block 1 from an optimisation or capacity limit of these readers. A's departure and every net's middle-range sign stayed where they were (observed stability), while B's departure fell somewhat, with more first-reader-block attention on the labelled tokens.
- **Review:** Codex (GPT-6, `gpt-6-astra`) asked for five fixes, all done (`results/review_e77.md`):
  - (high) the residual gap and the A/B difference were assigned to block 1 ("set by block 1", "belongs mainly to block 1", "two measured parts"), which one reader fit per source cannot separate from an optimisation or capacity limit, with P312 failing on the best-validation weights: reworded to a source-associated difference that persists under this recipe, P313 and P314 as observed stability, also in the plain-words addition (which keeps the residual-stream caveat);
  - (medium) attention masses were read as re-gathering: reported as attention to the labelled-token positions, with re-pooling and direct reading as hypotheses;
  - (medium) "only difference" overstated the matching: the output head's initial draws differ from the one-block reader's (the first reader block's are the same);
  - (medium) the frozen block 1 comes from the sources' best-validation checkpoint (89,000 steps for s1, s5, s11) while the source baseline uses the end-of-schedule weights: stated (the fresh2 against fresh1 comparison is matched);
  - (low) the two E38 nets with a fully attending block-2 head have two of the three lowest gaps, not the two lowest (s9 0.0036): corrected.
  It confirmed the implementation and measures, the registered hashes, P311-P314's scoring on the final weights, the tables and the descriptive gains.
- **Decision for Kelvin:** none.

**What this says.**
- **The one-block reader is part of the limit.** On the same frozen block 1, with the same episodes and schedule (and a differently initialised output head), adding one reader block lowers the test-NLL gap to 0.56-0.77 of the one-block reader's in every source. E76's result that a new one-block reader reaches about the source's gap therefore reflected, under this recipe, the one-block reader class, not only block 1's representation. Because block 1's residual stream still carries each labelled token's own input, this does not show that block 1 keeps all the information; it shows that a second block can use more of what block 1 leaves.
- **A source-associated difference persists.** With two reader blocks the B sources stay 1.8 times as far from Bayes as the A sources (sources: 2.0 times) on the registered end-of-schedule weights; on the validation-selected weights the ratio is 1.3, so the size of the persisting excess depends on the weight choice. With E69-E71 (more block-1 heads give the A allocation and about half the KL), this is compatible with the B excess being a block-1 allocation cost that more reader depth does not remove; with one reader fit per source it is not established.
- **The departure.** A's departure stays within 0.014 of the source's with a deeper reader, as with one reader block in E76 (observed stability); B's falls by about 0.03, and its first reader block attends more to the source's labelled tokens from the summary rows, compatible with the route E17 proposed for depth (gather transformed per-token evidence) without changing block 1, which an intervention would have to show. The middle-range sign that defines the type is kept in all ten.
- **Joint depth as a reference.** E38's jointly trained depth-3 nets reach similar gaps by their own type (A 0.0040, B 0.0097 against fresh2's 0.0045 and 0.0081) and lower departures (paired median change -0.051 against -0.020); their types differ from the sources' in several seeds, and their block 1 trained with the deeper reader for 90,000 steps in all, while fresh2's block 1 had its own 90,000 steps before. Post hoc, the two E38 nets with a block-2 head whose summary rows put all their attention on their own labelled tokens have two of the three lowest gaps (0.0027, 0.0038; s9 0.0036).
- **For M2 (why they cannot learn better).** In these two-layer nets, under this recipe, about a third of the remaining distance from Bayes is removed by one more reader block on a fixed block 1, and an A/B difference remains (1.8 times with the deeper reader on the registered weights). Whether the remainder is a limit of block 1's representation or of how such readers are trained is open; which computation of the second block recovers the third (re-pooling at the summary rows in B, a direct read of the labelled tokens in A, as the attention masses suggest) is not tested.
- **Limits.** One recipe and width; one fresh reader per source; two reader blocks only (the dev three-block runs gave 0.0044 and 0.0065, not registered); the end-of-schedule weights are registered and P312 depends on that choice; the frozen block 1 comes from the sources' best-validation checkpoint (89,000 steps for s1, s5, s11) while the source baseline uses their 90,000-step weights; joint3 differs in device, episode stream, training budget and type; attention masses do not establish what the reader blocks compute; test-NLL gaps without uncertainty estimates; 10 sources sharing E37's seeds.
