## Update 89 (2026-11-01 20:17Z): E78, a linear probe of block 1's summary rows departs from a source's own-error posterior over its noise level 2.6-5.2 times more in B than in A nets (P315), the departure ranks the test-NLL gap (P316), probes that add the labelled tokens remove most of B's excess (P317) and given membership halves it (P318) (amendment 86)

**TL;DR**
- **Design (CPU, existing nets).** For the 202 acquired nets of 18 cohorts (E72's 13 including uni, E38's depth-3 cohorts, E71's three layouts), 20,000 simulated world-1 episodes in each net's own format through its own forward; for each of the 60,000 sources the block-1 output of its summary row (hs[1]) is the probe input and its noise level (three levels) the target. Probes fit on 2/3 of the sources and scored on 1/3: logistic regression on the summary row (summ_lin, primary), boosted trees on it, logistic regression on the summary row with its four labelled tokens (summlab), and on the summary row's input embedding (emb). Scores: CE (held-out log loss on the true levels), KLL (mean KL from the source's own-error posterior over its level to the probe's; registered primary) and KLB (the same from the full Bayes posterior's marginal, which also uses the other sources' readings). KLL and KLB are probe discrepancies from a reference posterior, not measured information losses: a summary row can carry more than the own errors (KLL > 0 then even for a perfect probe), and the probe's capacity and calibration contribute. References: CE of the full posterior 0.448, of the own-error posterior 0.492, of the prior 1.099; a logistic probe on the raw errors, their squares and the reading reaches KLL 0.0002. Every net's recomputed test gap equals its registered one (largest difference 0.0).
- **P315 holds.** The B nets' median KLL is 2.6-5.2 times the A nets' in all 5 registered cohorts: ctrl 0.143 against 0.036 (3.9), w64ctrl 0.126 against 0.027 (4.7), w128ctrl 0.121 against 0.023 (5.2), h2w8 0.151 against 0.039 (3.9), h3w16 0.152 against 0.058 (2.6).
- **P316 holds.** Over the 94 acquired nets of ctrl, fix, nocons, h4, b1h4, h2w8, h3w16 and h4w16, Spearman(registered gap, KLL) = 0.60; within cohorts 0.59-0.83 in ctrl, fix, h4, h2w8, h3w16, h4w16, 0.50 in nocons, 0.01 in b1h4.
- **P317 holds (registered: 32 of 33).** In 32 of 33 B nets of P315's cohorts KLL(summlab) <= 0.6 x KLL; the exception, w64ctrl s2, has an infinite summlab KL because a float32 probe probability underflowed to zero. Post hoc in float64 its summlab KLL is 0.050, which would make it 33 of 33 (E78.3).
- **P318 holds.** E60's own nets' median KLL is 0.019, 0.52 of E37's ctrl A nets' 0.036.
- **Descriptive.** CE gives the same picture without a reference posterior (ctrl A 0.503, ctrl B 0.571; post hoc Spearman with the gap 0.83 over P316's nets, 0.63 within its A nets). Of the 15 nets in which no block-1 head meets the pooling criterion (summary-row attention mass on its own labelled tokens >= 0.5; E72's head counts), 10 have KLL 0.50-0.53, near the input embedding's 0.61 (ctrl s8, nocons s3, mag s3, w64mag s4, s5, s7, d3ctrl s0, s3, d3mag s3, fix s3), and 5 have 0.03-0.46 (fix s0 0.46, s9 0.37, s2 0.22, s6 0.09; w128mag s0, an A net, 0.03). Two depth-3 nets with a pooling head also have KLL 0.48-0.49 (d3ctrl s7, s8); they are the two whose block-2 summary rows attend fully to their own labelled tokens (E77) and among the closest to Bayes (gaps 0.0027, 0.0038), which fits block 2 doing their pooling (a hypothesis). The four-head A cohorts (h4, b1h4, h3w16, h4w16) have higher KLL than the two-head A nets (0.056-0.060 against 0.036) but lower KLB (0.032-0.038 against 0.053), which fits their summaries head bringing the other sources' readings into the summary row (post hoc). By cohort median the boosted probes score no better than the linear ones. Post hoc, KLB ranks the gap more closely than KLL (Spearman 0.82 over P316's nets; within its A nets 0.61 against 0.00). On E77's ten sources, KLL ranks the second reader block's absolute gain (Spearman 0.66), not its relative gain (0.13).
- **Sensitivity (post hoc, asked for by the review).** Refitting the primary probe with an episode-disjoint split (`e78x_epsplit.py`; 66 nets of P315's cohorts and own) changes KLL by a median of -0.0001 (range -0.004 to +0.011) and leaves the B/A ratios (4.0, 5.0, 5.2, 4.0, 2.8) and own's ratio to ctrl A (0.51) essentially unchanged.
- **What it shows.** How far a linear probe of a source's block-1 summary row is from the source's own-error posterior over its noise level separates the head allocations: 0.02-0.06 nats per source in A nets by cohort, about four times as much with the B allocation's single pooling head at widths 32-128 and with two or three heads, and about 0.5 in most nets with no head meeting the pooling criterion. The discrepancy and the probe's direct log loss rank the test-NLL gap across 94 content-routing nets of eight layouts (0.60 registered; 0.83 for CE and 0.82 for KLB, post hoc), and given membership halves the discrepancy. Probes that add the four labelled tokens' block-1 outputs come close to the own-error posterior in every cohort (B medians 0.050-0.063), so most of what B's summary row misses is linearly recoverable from the summary row together with those tokens. These are statements about linear recoverability from one row or five, not about what the net reads.
- **Review:** Codex (GPT-6, `gpt-6-astra`) asked for five fixes, all done (`results/review_e78.md`):
  - (high) KLL is a probe discrepancy from one reference posterior, not information destruction (the row can carry more than the own errors; the probe's capacity and calibration contribute): reworded throughout, with CE added as the direct measure and KLB kept descriptive, and causal "decides/sets" removed, also in the plain-words addition and the account sentences;
  - (high) the "no pooling head" grouping was made by KLL and omitted counterexamples (fix s6 0.089, w128mag s0 0.030): replaced by the full list of the 15 nets that meet no pooling criterion (P_h >= 0.5), with the threshold stated;
  - (medium) block-2 pooling in two depth-3 nets and the E77 link were read as mechanism: kept as hypotheses; the summary-plus-labelled probe is described as combined recoverability; the account's E77 sentence notes the weight choice;
  - (medium) the split is by sources, not episodes: disclosed, and an episode-disjoint check run (unchanged);
  - (medium) the float64 recheck reports lbfgs non-convergence warnings, the registered 32 of 33 is kept apart from the post hoc 33 of 33, and "every B net" and "boosted probes recover no more" are now cohort-median statements.
  It confirmed the target and marginal construction, the own-forward extraction, the loader dispatch, the 202 matching gaps, the hashes, the tables, P315-P318 and the reported correlations.
- **Decision for Kelvin:** none.

With float64 outputs the three infinite scores are finite (0.027-0.056), the summary-row scores agree with the registered float32 ones to 5e-4, and P317 would count 33 of 33.

**What this says.**
- **The allocation goes with how readable the reliability is at the summary row.** Across five content-routing cohorts at widths 32-128 and with two or three block-1 heads, a linear probe of the B allocation's summary row is 2.6-5.2 times further from the source's own-error posterior over its noise level than the A allocation's, and its direct log loss is higher (ctrl 0.571 against 0.503); in most nets with no head meeting the pooling criterion the probe does about as badly as from the input token alone. This is a probe-level counterpart of E63's head-allocation account: with the opposite-sign pair the summary row makes most of the own-error reliability information linearly readable; with one sign-dependent pooling head much less.
- **It ranks the distance from Bayes.** Over 94 signed content-routing nets the registered discrepancy ranks the test-NLL gap with Spearman 0.60 and within most cohorts 0.6-0.8; post hoc, the probe's direct log loss ranks it at 0.83 and the full-posterior discrepancy at 0.82, and within the A nets only those two carry the rank (0.63 and 0.61 against 0.00 for KLL). The four-head A nets illustrate why: their summary rows are further from the own-error posterior but closer to the full posterior (their summaries head), and they are closer to Bayes.
- **Where the rest is.** Probes of the summary row together with its four labelled tokens come close to the own-error posterior in every cohort (B medians 0.050-0.063), so after block 1 most of what B's summary row misses is linearly recoverable from those five rows; this is combined recoverability, not a measure of the labelled tokens alone. E77's second reader block gains most in absolute terms where the summary row's discrepancy is largest (Spearman 0.66 over its ten sources), compatible with, not evidence for, it reading that information.
- **Membership.** Told the membership, the learned pool's summary row is about twice as close to the own-error posterior as the A nets' content-routed one (0.019 against 0.036), in line with E60-E62's smaller KL and code dependence.
- **For M2 (why they deviate; predicting the KL from the architecture).** The head allocation now has a measured, probe-level consequence that separates the types across sizes and layouts and ranks the distance from Bayes across architectures: how readable each source's reliability is at its block-1 summary row. Whether the reader uses exactly this information, and how the pooling produces it (the cap, the norm term, the signed term), are not tested here.
- **Limits.** Linear and boosted probes of one row (or five), not the net's own read; KLL and KLB are discrepancies from reference posteriors; one simulation and one source-level split (the episode-disjoint check agrees); float32 probe outputs made three summlab KLs infinite (float64 recheck in E78.3, with non-convergence warnings); types are the registered middle-range signs (near zero in some depth-3 nets); the pooling criterion is an attention-mass threshold; the cohorts share seeds and initial values; the CE and KLB correlations and the depth-3 reading are post hoc.

- **What it shows.** Over training, how far a probe of the summary row is from the own-error posterior goes with the head allocation: the types' early distributions overlap; in each A lineage the interval containing the first persistent two-pooling-head checkpoint brings a larger proportional drop than the B lineages show over the same steps; the types separate from 10k on, while the last pairs form; and in four-head lineages that pair late the drop comes late. **What this says.**
- **The readability gain comes with the pair.** In every A lineage, the interval containing the first persistent two-pooling-head checkpoint brings a larger proportional drop in the summary row's probe discrepancy than the B lineages show over the same steps, and the A lineages then fall 2.4-2.8-fold within the next 6,000-8,000 steps; the four late-pairing four-head lineages stay at B levels until 40k-60k and drop then (their intervals span up to 20,000 steps). E79 counts pooling heads, not their signs; with E68 (every A lineage's pair has opposite signs when first seen, at E68's checkpoints) this is consistent with the information-side difference between the types arising when the second pooling head turns, which a coincidence in time does not prove.
- **Before the pair the types overlap.** While the first pooling heads form the two types' values overlap, and A lineages with one pooling head lie at or below the B range (s6 at 10k, s2 at 8k), so a one-head A lineage is already somewhat more readable than the B lineages; this fits, loosely, E68's finding that the median lineage first has B's allocation.
- **After the pair.** The A lineages keep improving to 80k (to 0.21-0.47 of their 10k value), compatible with E73's falling benchmark of the A pool, while the B lineages improve proportionally less (to 0.64-0.82, an 18-36% reduction), compatible with E73's nearly flat B benchmark. The B lineages' test gap halves over the same steps (0.055 to 0.026); which part of that the smaller probe improvement contributes is not identified (E73's B nets at fixed attention move further below their pool's benchmark, another candidate).
- **The cooldown.** During the final 10,000-step learning-rate decay every lineage's readability improves (9-18% in the ten lineages with a pooling head, 1.1% in s8), so part of the end-of-training sharpening is visible in block 1's summary statistic; a constant-rate control would be needed to attribute it to the decay.
- **For M2 (how they learn).** The probe-level consequence of the head allocation (E78) develops around a datable event in training, the persistent appearance of the second pooling head, in two- and four-head nets alike, and the types separate as the pairs form; this is the training-time side of the head-allocation account, as a timing association.
- **Limits.** A probe of one row (a discrepancy from one reference posterior, E78's review); one simulation and split; sparse checkpoints after 8,000 steps in E37 and throughout in E69 and E70 (a pair is dated at the next checkpoint); 4 A and 6 B lineages sharing E37's seeds; the pair rule depends on the attention-mass criterion.

**TL;DR**
- **Design (CPU, existing nets).** For the 114 acquired nets of 10 signed content-routing cohorts (ctrl, fix, nocons, h4, b1h4, w64ctrl, w128ctrl, h2w8, h3w16, h4w16), E78's 20,000 simulated episodes and split; per source a ladder of probe inputs along block 1: m2 (two numbers per pooling head: its own-key attention, renormalised, applied to E72's capped feature g and to s g, E72's M2), m3 (the renormalised own-key pooled value vectors, E72's M3), each pooling head's attention output (out_pool), all heads' outputs (out_all) and the summary row (summ); for nets with two pooling heads each head alone (m2_h, m3_h). Linear probes for all, boosted probes for m2, m3 and each head's m2. Score: KLL, E78's discrepancy from the own-error posterior over the noise level (not an information loss; probe-dependent across rungs). A2 = 71 A nets with exactly two pooling heads; B1 = 34 B nets with exactly one; 9 nets in neither (8 B nets with no pooling head; h3w16 s6, B with two).
- **P323 holds.** In 71 of 71 A2 nets the pair's boosted m2 KLL (0.015-0.026) is at most half of the better head's alone (0.147-0.229); the ratio is 0.10-0.13 (median 0.11).
- **P324 holds.** Over ctrl, w64ctrl, w128ctrl and h2w8, the B1 nets' median boosted m2 KLL is 0.191 and the A2 nets' median single-head value 0.195 (ratio 0.98; bar 0.7-1.3).
- **P325 holds.** In 71 of 71 A2 nets the pair's boosted m2 KLL is below the summary row's linear KLL plus 0.02 (in fact below the summary row's in all 71, by 0.004-0.050).
- **P326 holds.** The A2 nets' median boosted m2 KLL is 0.11-0.12 of the B1 nets' in all 4 two-head cohorts (ctrl 0.024 against 0.191, w64ctrl 0.020 against 0.172, w128ctrl 0.018 against 0.163, h2w8 0.023 against 0.206).
- **Descriptive.** Each A head's own pooled values read the same in every cohort with a linear probe (m3_h 0.385-0.387, fix 0.176), as do B's (0.39-0.41; fix 0.155); boosted probes of the pair's values come close to the pair's m2 (0.021-0.031). The heads' outputs (out_pool, linear) read as the pair's linear m3 (0.12-0.15 in A), and the summary row much better (A 0.023-0.060, B 0.121-0.255): the post-attention computation makes the information linearly readable. In the four-head A cohorts the summary row (0.056-0.060) is further from the own-error posterior than the pair's m2 (0.022), consistent with E78's reading (their summaries head bringing in the other sources' readings), not tested along this ladder. With fixed codes the pooling rungs are more readable (fix A single heads 0.15-0.18 and the pair 0.012-0.017; fix B's head 0.139-0.155), but fix B's summary row is not (0.245 against ctrl B's 0.143). The same picture holds in CE (A2: pair 0.510, single heads 0.690, summary row 0.488; B1: head 0.681, summary row 0.571).
- **What it shows.** The probe-level difference between the types (E78) is already visible in the four numbers constructed from the A type's two opposite-sign pooling heads (E72's M2: their own-key attention applied to a capped-feature proxy): a boosted probe of each head's pair of numbers alone is about as far from the own-error posterior as one of a B net's single head (0.15-0.23), and of the pair's four numbers about a tenth as far, in every one of 71 A nets of 10 layouts, widths 32-128 and two to four heads. This is complementary recoverability under these probes, consistent with the account's partner hypothesis (E63, E66), not a test of necessity or of the net's own read.
- **Review:** Codex (GPT-6, `gpt-6-astra`) asked for five fixes, all done (`results/review_e80.md`):
  - (high) "cannot", "is set by" and "B lacks the partner" read probe performance and matched aggregate medians as necessity and mechanism (E66's surgery is not partner removal): reworded to complementary recoverability under these probes, consistent with the partner hypothesis;
  - (high) the post-attention conclusion compared a boosted probe of a constructed four-number proxy with a linear probe of the summary row (which also holds the input residual): P325 is now reported operationally, without sufficiency or a cause for the better linear decoding after the block;
  - (medium) the plain-words "ten times more" and "as much as the summary token" turned discrepancy ratios into information (and CE favours the summary row): reworded as distances from the own-error answer, with the probe classes named;
  - (medium) "every rung is more readable" with fixed codes is false for fix B's summary row (0.245 against 0.143): restricted to the pooling rungs;
  - (medium) the four-head direction toward the full posterior is inferred: kept as consistent with E78.
  It confirmed the rung implementation (own-key renormalisation, g and s g, pooled values, single-head slicing, the summary-row attention outputs, the pooling criterion), the hashes, the tables and both 71-of-71 counts, and P323-P326's scoring.
- **Decision for Kelvin:** none.

**E80.2 Predictions**

| # | test | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| P323 | A2: boosted KLL(m2_pool) <= 0.5 x the better head's boosted KLL(m2_h), in >= 75% | holds: 71 of 71 (ratios 0.10-0.13) |
| P324 | two-head cohorts: median boosted KLL(m2) of B1 within +-30% of A2's single-head median | holds: 0.191 against 0.195 (0.98) |
| P325 | A2: boosted KLL(m2_pool) <= linear KLL(summ) + 0.02, in >= 75% | holds: 71 of 71 |
| P326 | A2 / B1 median boosted KLL(m2) <= 0.5 in >= 3 of 4 two-head cohorts | holds: 4 of 4 (0.11-0.12) |

**What this says.**
- **Consistent with a missing partner.** A boosted probe of a single pooling head's two attention-weighted capped features is about as far from the source's own-error posterior whether the head is one of A's pair or B's only pooling head (medians 0.195 and 0.191, aggregate medians, not a match of the statistics themselves); for A's two heads together the distance is about a tenth, in all 71 A nets. With E63 (A pools with an opposite-sign pair) and E66 (removing one head's signed term, a different intervention, raises A's sign dependence to B's level), this is consistent with the hypothesis that a single sign-dependent head recovers little of the even statistic Bayes uses and an opposite-sign pair recovers much more; it does not test necessity.
- **The summary row.** Operationally, the boosted probe of the pair's constructed four numbers is at least as close to the own-error posterior as the linear probe of the summary row in all 71 A nets (P325); the pair's numbers are a constructed proxy, not an intermediate activation, and the summary row also contains the input residual, so this neither shows that the four numbers are sufficient nor isolates what the output map and MLP do. Linear decoding is much better after the complete block than from the heads' raw outputs (0.12-0.15 against 0.02-0.06 in A). In the four-head cohorts the summary row is further from the own-error posterior than the pair's numbers, consistent with E78's reading (their summaries head bringing in the other sources' readings), which this ladder does not test.
- **For M2 (why the B type deviates more; predicting from the architecture).** This gives the head-allocation account a probe-level counterpart across ten layouts: how recoverable a source's reliability is from block 1's pooled numbers goes with whether the pooling has an opposite-sign partner. What the reader does with it, and the sign-level computation, are not probed here.
- **Limits.** Probe recoverability differs between rungs of different dimension and form; m2 uses E72's capped-feature proxy g (the token's centred norm ratio), not the net's value vectors; KLL is a discrepancy from one reference posterior; one simulation and split; the pooling criterion is an attention-mass threshold; 9 nets (8 without a pooling head) are outside the tested sets.

## Update 92 (2026-11-02 05:12Z): E81, restricting a B net's non-pooling block-1 head to the source's own labelled tokens during a second training cycle makes all six B nets A-type (P331) with 0.39-0.58 of an unrestricted second cycle's test-NLL gap (P330) and A's summary-row readability (P332), while the same restriction to another source's tokens does not help (P333) and A nets barely change (P334); the restricted head first pairs with opposite signs in all six (P327), but goes sign-neutral with a reversed departure in only two (P328, P329 and P335 fail) (amendment 89)

**TL;DR**
- **Design (CPU, retraining).** Sources: E37's six ctrl B nets with one pooling head (s4, s5, s7, s9, s10, s11) and four A nets (s0, s1, s2, s6). A second training cycle from the trained values, every parameter trainable, train_sw's schedule (1,000-step warmup to lr 1e-3, constant to 80,000, cooldown to 90,000; a fresh AdamW), on a new episode stream np.random.default_rng([seed + 8100, cid, 7]) shared by a source's arms, in three arms: cycle2 (the standard architecture); ownh (block 1's non-pooling head r may attend, from the three summary rows, only to the source's own four labelled tokens; r = head 0 for s4, head 1 for the other B nets and for the A nets); otherh (r restricted to the four labelled tokens of source (s + 1) mod 3; B only). 26 trainings. Evaluation (`e81_eval.py`, end-of-schedule weights for the runs and the sources): the test-NLL gap on tiny-pfn's 16,000 test episodes, rom_large and rom_middle on E12's pairs (type A if rom_middle < 0), E74's block-1 head measures (P_h, the signed coefficient K, the norm term at |r| = 3, pooling heads at P_h >= 0.5, an opposite-sign pair) at the end and at the stored checkpoints, E78's KLL, and r's mass on its target tokens (1.00 in all 16 restricted nets). u = the B source's original pooling head.
- **P327 holds.** At 5,000 steps all six B ownh nets have two pooling heads with opposite-sign K (|K_r| 1.69-2.17 against |K_u| 1.67-2.44); r's K already has the sign opposite to u's at the 2,000-step checkpoint in all six. The restricted head meets the pooling criterion by construction (P_h = 1), so this tests the sign.
- **P328 fails.** At 90,000 steps |K_r| <= 0.25 |K_u| in 2 of 6 (s9 0.06, s11 0.10); in s4, s5, s7 and s10 the opposite-sign pair persists (|K_r| / |K_u| 0.53-0.64, within the A sources' 0.39-0.65). K and the norm term are E74's averages over the source's own labelled keys, computed from the query and key weights without the mask (only P_h uses the attention): for ownh's r these are the keys it attends to; for otherh's r they are keys it cannot attend to, so its K and norm term in E81.1 do not describe its pooling.
- **P329 fails.** r's norm term at |r| = 3 is positive with u's negative in 2 of 6 (s9 +4.0 against -6.9, s11 +5.2 against -7.7); in the other four r's is -0.4 to -0.8 (u's -3.8 to -3.9).
- **P330 holds.** gap(ownh) / gap(cycle2) is 0.39-0.58 in 6 of 6 (bar 0.75). The ownh B gaps (0.0038-0.0058, median 0.0052) are at the A nets' level (cycle2 0.0047-0.0064, median 0.0052; ownh 0.0042-0.0061).
- **P331 holds.** rom_middle(ownh) < 0 in 6 of 6 (-0.015 to -0.040); every cycle2 and otherh B net keeps rom_middle > 0 (+0.036 to +0.079).
- **P332 holds.** KLL(ownh) / KLL(cycle2) is 0.20-0.29 in 6 of 6 (ownh 0.027-0.035; A cycle2 0.032-0.034).
- **P333 holds.** gap(otherh) / gap(cycle2) is 1.09-1.24 in 6 of 6 (bar 0.90).
- **P334 holds.** On the A nets gap(ownh) / gap(cycle2) is 0.88-1.04 (4 of 4 within 0.15).
- **P335 fails.** rom_large(ownh) < 0 in 2 of 6, the two sign-neutral nets (s9 -0.132, s11 -0.145); the four with a persisting pair have small positive departures (0.023-0.039; A nets under cycle2 0.056-0.070).
- **Descriptive.** A second cycle alone lowers every source's gap to 0.76-0.90 of its source's end-of-schedule gap and converts no net (all six B nets keep one pooling head and rom_middle > 0). At step 0 either restriction disrupts the B nets (validation NLL 0.78-1.20 against 0.326-0.330 for cycle2) but not the A nets (0.322-0.326, their cycle2 level); ownh and otherh start alike and end apart. In the four paired ownh B nets u becomes a pure own-token pooler (P_h 0.985-0.987, its summaries mass 0.002-0.004, against 0.80-0.84 and 0.15-0.18 under cycle2 and otherh); in s9 and s11 P_h is 0.86-0.89 with 0.09-0.12 on other sources' labelled tokens. On the A nets ownh weakens r's norm term (-0.8 to -2.4 against -3.1 to -3.9 under cycle2) and lowers the departure in 3 of 4 (0.032-0.061 against 0.056-0.070).
- **Post hoc (trajectories, not registered).** r's own logit L_own, the norm-scaled part whose sign sets the norm term's sign, starts negative in all six B nets (-6.4 to -8.2, from its summaries-head role). In the four paired nets it crosses zero between 10,000 and 40,000 steps and ends at +2.2 to +3.8. In s9 and s11 it first falls to about -23 at 10,000-20,000 steps (r's norm term is already +5.3 and +4.0 at 5,000, against +1.6 to +2.4 in the paired nets), and r's K becomes small relative to u's from 40,000 steps (s9 +0.51 against +1.48 at 40,000 and +0.18 against +2.82 at 90,000; s11 -0.04 against -1.68, then -0.24 against -2.37); L_own ends at -7.3 and -10.6. On the A nets r's L_own falls from +16 to +22 to +3.9 to +10.6.
- **Dev runs (excluded).** After the registration the remaining dev runs on E43's newinit nets finished: ownh s2 kept the opposite-sign pair to 90,000 steps (K +1.33 against -2.25, r's norm term -0.6) with 0.39 of cycle2's gap, rom_large +0.025 and rom_middle -0.040; otherh s1 stayed B with 1.20 of cycle2's gap. With ownh s1 and s4 (sign-neutral, disclosed in the amendment), the dev runs went sign-neutral in 2 of 3; the registered thresholds for P328, P329 and P335 came from the two that had finished.
- **What it shows.** In this design, restricting a one-pooling-head B net's other block-1 head to its source's own labelled tokens for a second training cycle gives it a second pooling head, the A type, the A nets' test-NLL gap and the A nets' summary-row probe discrepancy; restricting the same head to another source's tokens, which disrupts the net as much at the start, does not, and on A nets, which already have the partner, the restriction changes the gap by at most 12%. The registered intervention succeeds (P330-P334), as the partner account predicts. It does not isolate the partner as the mediator: ownh also gives r the membership and removes its access to the summaries, every parameter is retrained, otherh matches the initial disruption but not the later adaptation, and the A nets show the restriction is harmless where a partner exists. The registered account of how the partner works failed: an opposite-sign pair forms first in all six and persists in four, while two nets end with a small relative signed coefficient for r, a positive norm term and a reversed departure, at a similar gap. These are two observed end states, both with a second pooling head; the dev route is not the typical one.
- **Review:** Codex (GPT-6, `gpt-6-astra`) asked for five fixes, all done (`results/review_e81.md`):
  - (high) the draft and the proposed account sentences attributed the rescue to the missing partner, but ownh also gives the head the membership and removes its access to the summaries, every parameter is retrained, otherh controls only the initial disruption, and the A nets do not isolate a mediator: reworded to a registered intervention that succeeds as the partner account predicts, without an identified mediator, with the two end states as observed endpoints; the membership caveat is kept in the plain-words conclusion, the status bullet and the account;
  - (medium) the second cycle starts from each source's best-validation `model.pt` (the 89,000-step weights for s1, s5 and s11), while the source rows and the "gap / source" denominators use the end-of-schedule weights: stated in the Setup, with the denominator named;
  - (medium) "lost" and "vanished" signed terms and a causal role for the norm term overstated averaged, unmasked own-key diagnostics (s9's K_r is +0.51 at 40,000 steps): reworded to a small relative mean signed coefficient, with the positive norm term and the reversed departure as associations; otherh's K and norm term are now marked as describing keys its restricted head cannot attend to;
  - (medium) the E79 sentence for the account said the discrepancy "falls most" in the pairing interval, while P319 compares that interval with the B lineages' drop over the same steps: restored to that comparison;
  - (low) the queue logs cannot establish the token failure or the absence of other writes: the failure is attributed to the coordinator and the absence of writes to the file modification times.
  It confirmed the mask, the shared episode stream, the schedule, the head choices, the end-of-schedule evaluation and the tabulated results, P327 and P330-P334 as holding and P328, P329 and P335 as failing as registered, and found the dev-run disclosure adequate.
- **Decision for Kelvin:** none.

**E81.3 Predictions**

| # | test | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| P327 | ownh B at 5k: two pooling heads with opposite-sign K, >= 5 of 6 | holds: 6 of 6 |
| P328 | ownh B at 90k: \|K_r\| <= 0.25 \|K_u\|, >= 4 of 6 | fails: 2 of 6 (s9, s11) |
| P329 | ownh B at 90k: norm term > 0 for r and < 0 for u, >= 4 of 6 | fails: 2 of 6 (s9, s11) |
| P330 | gap(ownh) <= 0.75 gap(cycle2), >= 5 of 6 B | holds: 6 of 6 (0.39-0.58) |
| P331 | rom_middle(ownh) < 0, >= 5 of 6 B | holds: 6 of 6 |
| P332 | KLL(ownh) <= 0.5 KLL(cycle2), >= 5 of 6 B | holds: 6 of 6 (0.20-0.29) |
| P333 | gap(otherh) >= 0.90 gap(cycle2), >= 5 of 6 B | holds: 6 of 6 (1.09-1.24) |
| P334 | A: \|gap(ownh) / gap(cycle2) - 1\| <= 0.15, >= 3 of 4 | holds: 4 of 4 (0.88-1.04) |
| P335 | rom_large(ownh) < 0, >= 4 of 6 B | fails: 2 of 6 (s9, s11) |

**What this says.**
- **An intervention test of the partner account.** E63-E80 found that B nets pool with one sign-dependent head and keep the other on the summaries, and that A's opposite-sign pair goes with a more readable summary row; all of that was correlational or probe-level. Here a B net given a second own-token pooling head during further training reaches the A nets' gap, type and readability, while a restriction of the same head that starts from the same disruption but points it at another source's tokens does not, and A nets are not harmed by it. The registered outcome (P330-P334 hold) is what the partner account predicts. It is intervention efficacy, not an identified mediator: ownh also gives r the membership (it does not have to find its source's tokens) and removes its access to the summaries (as otherh does), the whole net is retrained, and otherh controls the initial disruption, not the downstream adaptation. Nor does it say why B training does not form a content-routed partner (E68: the second head's turn, which B lineages never make).
- **Two end states.** The registered mechanism, that the supplied head settles into a sign-neutral, norm-term pooling as in two dev runs, failed (P328, P329, P335: 2 of 6). In four nets the A nets' opposite-sign pair forms and stays, with K ratios inside A's range; in two the head first pairs, then its own logit turns strongly negative and its norm term strongly positive, its mean signed coefficient becomes small relative to u's, and the departure is reversed (-0.13, -0.15); that the positive norm term produces the reversal is an association here, not a shown mediation. Both end states reach similar gaps (0.0038-0.0058 against 0.0045 and 0.0050), so in these nets the gap does not fix the departure's sign. Why the two nets took the second route is not identified (r's norm term was already larger at 5,000 steps).
- **The departure with a routing-free partner (descriptive).** In the four paired nets the departure (0.023-0.039) is below the A nets' after cycle2 (0.056-0.070), with r's norm term close to zero (-0.4 to -0.8) instead of A's -3 to -4; on the A nets the restriction weakens r's norm term and lowers the departure in 3 of 4. This fits E63 and E60 (a head free of content routing lacks the large negative norm term, and membership-given nets have a small departure), as an association in 10 nets.
- **For M2 (why the B type deviates; how they learn).** The head-allocation account's central claim about B, that its excess comes from lacking a second pooling head, now has a training-time intervention consistent with it (supplying one, told its source's tokens, removes B's excess in these six nets), not yet one that isolates the partner; E82 tests whether E72's benchmark of the pool follows the departure through it, including the reversal.
- **Limits.** One schedule (a second full cycle from the trained values); 6 B and 4 A sources sharing E37's seeds; the restriction applies from the summary rows only; ownh and cycle2 start from different losses (otherh is the matched-disruption control); the type label is the middle-range sign and the pooling rule an attention-mass threshold (met by r by construction); KLL is a probe discrepancy (E78); the dev runs (two finished at registration) set the thresholds.

Files: `train_more.py`, `pfn_ownh.py`, `e81_eval.py`, `e81_summ.py`, `e81_loop.sh`; `runs/e81/<arm>_s<seed>` (26 runs with `ckpt/`), dev `runs/e81x`; `results/e81/*.json`, `results/e81.json`, `results/e81_tables.md`, dev `results/e81x/*.json`, `results/review_e81.md`; logs `runs/e81/*.log`, `results/e81_eval.log`, `results/e81_loop.log`, `results/e81_summ.log`.

## Update 93 (2026-11-02 05:16Z): E82, E72's factorised benchmark of block 1's own pool (M3) has the sign of the departure in all 36 of E81's nets and sources (P336, a weak bar) and is negative in both reversed nets at about 0.37 of their departure (P339), is within 0.03 of the departure in all 16 opposite-sign-pair nets (P337) and at least 1.5 times it in all 18 one-pooling-head nets (P338), and the reversed nets' cap scale is 0.38-0.40 of their unrestricted second cycle's (P340) (amendment 90)

**TL;DR**
- **Design (CPU, E81's nets).** E81's 26 second-cycle nets and their 10 sources, end-of-schedule weights. Per net (`e82_cb.py`, E72's computation with pfn_ownh's loader): E72's classifier-estimated, factorised constrained-Bayes benchmarks of the source's own block-1 pool (the pooled statistic held fixed), M1 (the reduced pooling model), M2 (two numbers per pooling head) and M3 (the renormalised own-key pooled value vectors; boosted classifiers on 200,000 simulated episodes, numpy seed 7201), the cap scale c, the recomputed rom and detq (rom with the summary rows' block-1 queries detached). Classes from E81's head measures: pair (two pooling heads with opposite-sign K; 16 nets: the 4 A sources, their cycle2 and ownh nets, and the 4 paired ownh B nets), single (one pooling head; 18: the 6 B sources, their cycle2 and otherh nets), neutral (an ownh B net with two pooling heads and |K_r| <= 0.25 |K_u|; 2: ownh s9 and s11). E72's decomposition rom = M3 + (detq - M3) + (rom - detq).
- **P336 holds, on a weak bar.** sign(M3) = sign(rom_large) in 36 of 36 (bar 90%). Since 34 of the 36 departures are positive, the bar would also be met if both reversed nets had a positive M3; their sign is tested by P339.
- **P337 holds.** |M3 - rom_large| <= 0.03 in 16 of 16 pair nets (largest 0.017).
- **P338 holds.** M3 >= 1.5 x rom_large in 18 of 18 single nets (ratios 2.8-3.9; M3 0.41-0.46 against departures 0.11-0.16).
- **P339 holds (2 nets).** In both neutral nets M3 < 0 and |M3| < |rom_large|: -0.048 against -0.132 (s9) and -0.056 against -0.145 (s11), 0.36 and 0.39 of the departure.
- **P340 holds (2 nets).** The neutral nets' cap scale is 0.38 and 0.40 of their source's cycle2 net's (1.53 against 4.02; 1.77 against 4.44); every other net has c 3.54-4.71.
- **Descriptive.** The identity rom = M3 + (detq - M3) + (rom - detq) holds per net; medians of each term by class (medians do not add up exactly): pair rom 0.056, M3 0.053, detq - M3 +0.039, rom - detq -0.037 (the two reading parts opposite and largely cancelling in every pair net, +0.021 to +0.058 and -0.022 to -0.043, as in E72's A nets); single rom 0.140, M3 0.433, detq - M3 -0.248, rom - detq -0.043 (the nets at fixed summary-row attention far below the benchmark, E72's B pattern); neutral rom -0.139, M3 -0.052, detq - M3 -0.084, rom - detq -0.003 (a small query term, -0.004 and -0.003, against -0.022 to -0.063 in every other net). As in E72, detq - M3 also contains other routes and the benchmark's own error. M2 has M3's sign in every net; M1 (the reduced pooling model) is about zero in the pair nets (-0.011 to +0.018; negative in 7 of 16). Post hoc and descriptive, within the 16 pair nets M3 follows the departure over 0.023-0.096 (Pearson 0.91, Spearman 0.91; 16 related nets from 10 source lineages, not independent replications); the four B nets given a partner have the four lowest benchmarks (0.016-0.029; departures 0.023-0.039).
- **Plumbing.** The recomputed rom equals E81's in all 36. For the 7 sources whose registered E72 checkpoint is the 90,000-step weights, E82 reproduces E72's registered M3, c and rom; s1, s5 and s11 differ slightly (for example s1 M3 0.073 against 0.081) because E72 used their 89,000-step best-validation weights.
- **Dev nets (excluded; disclosed in the amendment).** On E81's dev nets the two sign-neutral ownh nets had M3 -0.041 and -0.053 against departures -0.131 and -0.108 and c 1.27 and 1.57, and set the thresholds of P339 and P340; the registered pair reproduces that pattern.
- **What it shows.** E72's benchmark of the source's own block-1 pool, computed from the pooled values alone, agrees with the departure through E81's intervention: positive and close in size in every net with an opposite-sign pair (including the B nets given a partner, which have the smallest benchmarks), positive and about three times the departure in every one-head net, and negative in the two nets where the supplied head went sign-neutral and the departure reversed. In those two the benchmark has the right sign and about 0.37 of the size; the residual is in detq - M3 (about -0.08), and unlike every other net their query term is about zero. The direction of the departure is therefore visible in the benchmark of block 1's pool even where a within-source intervention reverses it. This is numerical agreement, not mediation (E81 retrains the whole net), and it rests on two registered nets; the two dev nets that set the thresholds showed the same pattern.
- **Review:** Codex (GPT-6, `gpt-6-astra`) asked for four fixes, all done (`results/review_e82.md`):
  - (high) the plain words called M3 an exact Bayes reader, and several sentences had the pool setting the departure's direction and size or the decomposition supplying causal fractions, while M3 is classifier-estimated and factorised with the statistic held fixed, detq - M3 contains other routes and the benchmark's error (Update 82), and E81 retrains the whole net: reworded to a classifier-estimated benchmark whose sign, and in pair nets size, agree with the departure, with residuals instead of fractions and no mediation claim;
  - (medium) the class medians were written as additive equations, but medians do not add up (single: 0.142 against a median rom of 0.140): now listed term by term, with the identity stated per net;
  - (medium) "a cap this strong would by itself give a positive departure" carried E58's uniform-pool, frozen-embedding result over to learned pools: now E58's nets, in a different design, had positive departures at comparable cap scales, with the coexistence kept and no mechanism named;
  - (low) "no query term" (the residuals are -0.004 and -0.003) became a small query term; the two registered reversed nets are kept separate from the two threshold-setting dev nets; the 0.91 correlation is labelled descriptive (16 related nets from 10 lineages).
  It confirmed the end-of-schedule loading, the ownh masks, the matching pooling lists, all 36 recomputed roms, the tables, classes and P336-P340, the correlations and the seven exact matches to E72's registered source values (the s1, s5 and s11 differences disclosed), and found the amendment's correction, its conflicting time labels and the unattended run disclosed consistently with the hashes and logs (which cannot prove what was not seen).

**E82.2 Predictions**

| # | test | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| P336 | sign(M3) = sign(rom_large), >= 90% of nets with a pooling head | holds: 36 of 36 (34 positive; a weak bar) |
| P337 | pair nets: \|M3 - rom_large\| <= 0.03, >= 75% | holds: 16 of 16 (largest 0.017) |
| P338 | single nets with rom_large > 0: M3 >= 1.5 x rom_large, >= 75% | holds: 18 of 18 (2.8-3.9) |
| P339 | neutral nets: M3 < 0 and \|M3\| < \|rom_large\|, >= 75% | holds: 2 of 2 |
| P340 | neutral nets: c <= 0.6 x c of the same source's cycle2 net, >= 75% | holds: 2 of 2 (0.38, 0.40) |

**What this says.**
- **The sign through a reversal.** E81's sign-neutral partner reversed the departure in two nets; the benchmark of their own pool turned negative with it, while it stayed positive in all 34 other nets. So the direction of the departure is visible in the benchmark of block 1's pool. With E63's reading (the pooling's norm term sets how large errors are weighted) this goes with r's norm term, +4.0 and +5.2 in those two nets against -0.4 to -7.7 in the other 52 pooling heads of the 36 nets (E81): an association in two nets, not a test of mediation. The benchmark's size agrees only for the pair nets.
- **The pair nets.** As in E72's A nets, the benchmark is close to the departure as an offset of two reading parts of opposite sign; it also follows the departure down to the B nets given a partner (post hoc, Pearson 0.91 over 16 related nets, most of the range coming from E81's intervention), so in this set the departure's size goes with the pool's benchmark where the pool is an opposite-sign pair.
- **The single nets.** Unchanged by a second cycle or by the otherh restriction: M3 stays at about three times the departure and the nets at fixed attention stay about 0.25 below it (E72, E73), so the B nets' departure is not the benchmark's in any of the 18.
- **The reversed nets.** The benchmark is about 0.37 of their departure; the residual at fixed attention (detq - M3) is about -0.08 and the query term about zero (E72's operational decomposition, not a causal split). Their cap scale (1.5-1.8, against 3.5-4.7 in the other 34 nets) is low. E58's uniform-pool nets, in a different design (frozen embedding, fixed weights), had positive departures at comparable cap scales (0.22 at c = 1, 0.12 at c = 2); here the strong cap coexists with a reversed departure, next to a pooling head whose norm term favours large errors, and which mechanism dominates is not identified (two nets).
- **For M2 (predicting the departure from the architecture).** A benchmark built from block 1's pooled values alone agrees with the departure's sign across E81's intervention, and with its size where the A allocation's pair exists; with E81 this associates the three observed end states (pair, single, sign-neutral partner) with three distinct patterns of benchmark and departure.

**What this says.**
- **An acquisition barrier, supported but not established.** E68 found that B lineages never turn their second head into a pooling head. E81 supplied one by restriction. Here, after the restriction is lifted, a head that had paired with the opposite sign ended content-routed in 3 of 4 sources: its routing logit rose from about 0 to about +17, the A heads' range. These nets ended with the A type, an end-of-schedule gap comparable to their E81 ownh endpoint, and A's readability. A content-routed partner is therefore attainable under this curriculum in these B nets, which supports the hypothesis that their deficit lies in forming the partner. It does not show that this is why ordinary B training fails, since all parameters adapt for 70,000 more updates. The fourth paired partner (s5) lost the competition with the summaries over 25k-40k, so keeping a partner is not guaranteed. Why s5 differs is not identified (at 20k its summaries mass was the highest of the four paired heads, 0.34 against 0.20-0.24).
- **The sign-neutral partners.** They had moved their own logit to about -22 under the restriction, and without the mask they attend to the summaries; they reverted at once. The partners' end state under the restriction goes with whether they were kept (paired: 3 of 4; sign-neutral: 0 of 2). The classes are E81's outcomes, so this is a comparison of outcomes, not of randomised conditions.
- **What the B nets' partners rely on.** At evaluation they need the mask: by the registered threshold the six B partners do not route by content, while E81's A nets' restricted heads keep 0.38-0.90 of their mass on their own tokens. The paired ones need their signed term, and the sign-neutral ones barely do (1.00-1.08x), as their K values imply. Every net needs u's signed term. Surgery far from the trained operating point shows dependence, not the mechanism (E66).
- **The departure.** The branches that end with a content-routed partner have the routing logit's negative norm term (-2.9 to -3.0) and an A-sized departure (0.055-0.069), while the restricted branches of the same sources ended with a small departure (0.023-0.039) and a near-zero norm term. This matches E63's association between routing and the departure within sources, but it compares the endpoints of two branches, not departures measured before and after the release, and it is not a mediation test. E72's benchmark again follows the outcome (within 0.01 in the kept nets; about three times the departure in the reverted ones).
- **For M2 (how they learn; why the B type deviates).** In these nets the head-allocation account's B deficit is consistent with a failure to form the second pooling head in training rather than an inability to keep a content-routed one (an acquisition barrier, supported, not established). This points at the early pairing window (E68, E79) as where B and A part, and suggests testing a transient restriction from the start of training.
- **Limits.** One release time (20,000 steps) and one schedule. Six B sources sharing E37's seeds, with 4 paired and 2 sign-neutral sources whose classes are E81's outcomes. The thresholds come from three dev runs truncated at 40,000 steps without the cooldown. Evaluation-time surgery is far from the trained operating point. The pooling criterion is an attention-mass threshold, and the weights are end-of-schedule.

**TL;DR**

Their validation never returned to its best, which was reached before the release (9k-10k).

They motivated the thresholds; the registered runs replicate the registered tests on six seeds that were selected as B, with one conversion that the dev runs did not show, and say nothing about conversion rates in general.
- **What it shows.** This particular early restriction did not by itself convert B initialisations. It covered updates 1-10,000, part of E68's 5,000-20,000 pairing window, and the forced pooler did not route by content (own-token mass 0.16-0.32 without the mask at 10k). The release was a large shock (s4's validation NLL went from 0.342 at 10k to 0.461 at 11k). In five of six, the unrestricted head took the summaries job while the restriction held; after the release the nets stayed B, four with the roles swapped and one with a split second head, at a worse gap than ordinary training. The single conversion (s9) is the seed whose other head had the lowest summaries mass at the release (0.33, down from 0.68 at 2k). That the summaries job, once held by one of two heads, keeps an initialisation in the B allocation is a hypothesis from six outcome-selected seeds and one conversion, not a test.
- **Review:** Codex (GPT-6, `gpt-6-astra`) asked for four fixes, all done (`results/review_e84.md`):
  - (high) "five role swaps" overstated P355, which holds in four (s11's second head ends split, with summaries mass 0.215 and own-token mass 0.354): the title, the plain words, the status bullet and the account now say that all five stayed B, four with the roles swapped;
  - (high) the mechanism outran the intervention. The restriction covers updates 1-10,000, only part of E68's 5,000-20,000 pairing window; the forced pooler does not route by content (own-token mass 0.16-0.32 at 10k); the release is a large shock; and neither E83 (a different training history and release time) nor E64 (a permanent bar) isolates early commitment. Now described as this particular early restriction and its release, with the summaries-job reading kept as a hypothesis that does not contradict E83's narrower finding;
  - (medium) "had not yet settled on the summaries" missed s9's reversal (its other head's summaries mass fell from 0.68 at 2k to 0.33 at the release): now "the lowest summaries mass at the release";
  - (medium) the smoke comparison covered 1,500 updates, the queue log shows a gap in this lane's jobs rather than the session's inactivity or its cause, and three truncated dev runs plus six outcome-selected seeds support the registered replication, not conversion rates or a mechanism: scoped accordingly.
  It confirmed the reconstruction of E37's recipe and stream, the restriction's scope and timing, the evaluation without the mask, the hashes, the tables and the scoring of P351-P356, the agreement of the CPU controls with E37, the single conversion and the five worse gaps.
- **Decision for Kelvin:** none.

**E84.3 Predictions**

| # | test | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| P351 | step 0 of all 12 runs equals E37's initial weights | holds: 12 of 12 (difference 0) |
| P352 | ctrl: rom_middle > 0 and one pooling head, >= 4 of 6 | holds: 6 of 6 |
| P353 | tr: C_h(u) >= 0.5 at 10k, >= 4 of 6 | holds: 5 of 6 (s9 0.33) |
| P354 | tr: rom_middle > 0 at 90k, >= 4 of 6 | holds: 5 of 6 (s9 A) |
| P355 | tr: P_h(r) >= 0.5 and C_h(u) >= 0.5 at 90k, >= 4 of 6 | holds: 4 of 6 (s9 both pool; s11 u split) |
| P356 | gap(tr) >= 0.9 x gap(ctrl), >= 4 of 6 | holds: 5 of 6 (1.17-2.92; s9 0.76) |

**What this says.**
- **This early restriction did not convert five of six B initialisations.** While r was restricted to pooling, the unrestricted head did not become a second pooling head; it took the summaries job, in s4, s5 and s7 within the first 2,000-5,000 updates. After the release the restricted head stayed the single pooling head in four nets, so they kept B's allocation with the roles swapped, worse than ordinary training; in s11 the second head ended split. This does not contradict E83's narrower finding (a partner formed under a restriction in a second training cycle was kept in three of four). The two designs differ in training history and release time, and in E81's second cycle no head was doing the summaries job at the release (the restricted head had been the summaries head), whereas here the other head had taken it.
- **The single conversion.** s9 is the seed whose u had the lowest summaries mass at the release (0.33, against 0.58-0.95). Its u had moved toward the summaries early (0.68 at 2k) and then partly away (0.52 at 5k). Both heads then pooled within 2,000 updates with opposite signs, and the net ended A, closer to Bayes than its control (0.76) and with E72's benchmark matching its departure (0.098 against 0.105). One seed is an observation, not an estimate of how often this happens.
- **Two kinds of failure.** When r had developed a signed term under the restriction (s5, s7), the swapped B net is an ordinary B net (KLL and M3 as the controls'), with a gap 1.2-1.7 times the control's. When r stayed sign-neutral (s4, s10, s11), it became a weak, sign-neutral single pooler. Those nets ended worst, with a gap 2.0-2.9 times the control's, a large departure, a low cap scale and validation that never recovered its pre-release best: a single sign-neutral pooler is a poor B solution, compared with E81's sign-neutral partner, which had a second, signed pooling head beside it.
- **For M2 (how they learn; why the B type deviates).** With E83, the results go with a hypothesis, not established, that the B allocation is held in place by a head holding the summaries job, not only by a missing pooling partner: a partner was kept when the summaries job had no head (E83), and was not formed here while the job was held (E84). A transient bar on the summaries job through the pairing window would test this more directly. E64 barred it permanently, giving 11 of 12 A nets, which cannot isolate early commitment.
- **Limits.** Six seeds and one restriction length (10,000 updates). The restricted head was chosen from the GPU-trained net's allocation. The release causes a large disruption. The dev runs (three, truncated at 40,000 without the cooldown) set the thresholds. Attention-mass criteria; end-of-schedule weights. The comparison with E83 sets two designs side by side (a second cycle against an ordinary training), not one manipulation.

## Update 96 (2026-11-02 18:58Z): E85, barring block 1's summaries job for the first 10,000 updates makes all six B initialisations A (P358, P359: 6 of 6, the registered rule's "supports H"), at 0.44-0.70 of their controls' gap (P360), with no head taking the reopened job at the measured checkpoints (P361); their end states are close to E64's permanent bar's (amendment 93)

**TL;DR**
- **Design (CPU, training; coordinator-approved, at most 2 heavy processes; registered before any run, without dev runs).** E37's six B seeds (s4, s5, s7, s9, s10, s11) were retrained with `train_nc.py --bar_until 10000`: train_sw.py's ctrl recipe from E37's initial weights and stream. For updates 1-10,000, block 1 is E64's nocons variant (both heads' summary rows barred from the other sources' summary tokens); from update 10,001, pfn2's standard forward.
  - Controls: E84's unrestricted CPU retrains of the same seeds.
  - Evaluation as in E84: `e81_eval.py` on the end-of-schedule weights; `e85_eval.py` (trajectory without the bar, the state under the bar at 10k, identity checks); `e82_cb.py` (descriptive).
  - The hypothesis H (Update 95): a head holding the summaries job keeps the net in B.
  - The registered rule (P359): A-converted (A type and two opposite-sign pooling heads) in >= 4 of 6 supports H; <= 1 of 6 (E84's rate) refutes it; 2-3 is undecided; uninformative if the manipulation check (P358) fails.
- **P357 holds.** Every run's step-0 weights equal E37's initial weights, and its 2k, 3k, 5k and 10k checkpoints equal E64's nocons checkpoints of the seed exactly (max abs difference 0), 6 of 6.
- **P358 holds (manipulation check).** At 10k, under the bar, both heads pool in 6 of 6 (P_h 0.62-0.95). Their K have opposite signs in all six (|K| 2.6-3.2 on the larger side), and their routing logits are +10 to +14 (s7: +2.7 and +10.1).
- **P359 supports H.** All 6 of 6 are A-converted at 90k: rom_middle -0.035 to -0.052, two pooling heads (P_h 0.985-0.993) with opposite-sign K, and KLL 0.036-0.041 (the controls 0.127-0.147).
- **P360 holds.** gap(nc) / gap(ctrl) is 0.44, 0.70, 0.47, 0.52, 0.53 and 0.53 (s4, s5, s7, s9, s10, s11), with gaps 0.0055-0.0081.
- **P361 holds.** At 11k, 1,000 updates after the reopening and measured without the bar, both heads' summaries mass is at most 0.06 in all six (checkpoints sampled at 11k, 12k, 15k, 20k, 40k, 60k and 90k).
- **Descriptive.**
  - Measured without the mask at the stored checkpoints, both heads met the pooling criterion by 5k in five seeds (P_h 0.67-0.85, opposite-sign K); s7 met it between 5k and 10k.
  - The reopening caused at most a small, brief rise in the validation gap (s9: 0.036 at 10k, 0.057 at 12k, 0.031 at 13k; s4 none).
  - The end states are close to E64's permanent bar's: gaps within 0.0002 (E64 0.0055-0.0083), rom_large within 0.0006 and rom_middle within 0.003 (s7 0.0029). E64's evaluation used its best-validation weights, the 90,000-step weights except in s11 (89,000). E72's benchmark M3 is 0.069-0.085 against departures of 0.074-0.101, the pair pattern, and the cap scale is 4.1-4.5.
  - E84's arms for comparison: the transient restriction of one head converted 1 of 6, and the unrestricted retrains 0 of 6.
- **What it shows.** A 10,000-update bar sufficed for these six selected initialisations. All six formed A's opposite-sign pair under the bar, no head took the reopened job at the measured checkpoints, and all ended A, with end states close to those of E64's permanent bar. By the registered rule this supports H, the early-allocation hypothesis. The literal prediction of its competitor H' (a return to B after the reopening) fails here; a broader, continuing pull of the summaries job is not excluded. The bar changes both heads' attention and the whole net's subsequent learning, so this shows that an early bar is sufficient, not a unique mediator, a necessary window or an irreversible decision. This is six outcome-selected seeds, one bar length, and a manipulation whose permanent version (E64) was known beforehand to make these seeds A.
- **Review:** Codex (GPT-6, `gpt-6-astra`) asked for four fixes, all done (`results/review_e85.md`):
  - (high) "the B type is decided by occupation before 10k" turned registered support into a causal claim. The bar changes both heads' attention and the whole net's later learning, and one duration shows sufficiency, not a unique mediator, a necessary window or an irreversible decision. The Update, the plain words and the account now say that a 10,000-update bar sufficed for these six selected initialisations, which supports the early-allocation hypothesis; H' fails in its literal form (a return to B), and a broader continuing pull is not excluded;
  - (medium) the equivalence with E64's permanent bar was overstated and one bound was false. s7's rom_middle differs by 0.0029, not within 0.002, and E64's evaluation used its best-validation weights (89,000 updates in s11). Now "close to", with the bounds 0.0002 (gap), 0.0006 (rom_large) and 0.003 (rom_middle), the weight selection disclosed, and "no further difference" removed;
  - (medium) sampled checkpoints were presented as a continuous history: "no head took the job" is now qualified as at the measured checkpoints, and s7's pairing as on the unmasked criterion;
  - (low) transcription: the s9 numbers are validation gaps, not NLL, and s7's control P_h is 0.80/0.00. Both corrected, and the smoke difference (0.08) is now logged in `results/e85x_smoke.log`.
  It confirmed the training and reopening implementation, the evaluator's masks, the scoring of P357-P361 and P359's "supports H", the tables otherwise, the registration hashes, the smoke checkpoints' byte-equality and their divergence after the reopening, and that the scheduler kept two jobs at most (`results/s7t.log`).
- **Decision for Kelvin:** none.

**E85.3 Predictions**

| # | test | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| P357 | step 0 = E37's initial weights; 2k-10k = E64's nocons checkpoints, 6 of 6 | holds: 6 of 6 (difference 0) |
| P358 | under the bar at 10k both heads pool, >= 4 of 6 | holds: 6 of 6 |
| P359 | A-converted at 90k: >= 4 of 6 supports H, <= 1 refutes, 2-3 undecided | 6 of 6: supports H |
| P360 | gap(nc) <= 0.9 x gap(ctrl), >= 4 of 6 | holds: 6 of 6 (0.44-0.70) |
| P361 | at 11k both heads' summaries mass < 0.5, >= 4 of 6 | holds: 6 of 6 (at most 0.06) |

**What this says.**
- **The registered test of H.** By the rule fixed before any run, 6 of 6 conversions support H. H' predicted a return to B once the job reopened (the summaries job pulling a head whenever it is available), and that did not happen here. With the job barred through the first 10,000 updates, both heads pooled with opposite signs, mostly by 5,000 on the unmasked criterion. When the job reopened, neither head took it at the measured checkpoints, and every net ended A.
- **Close to the permanent bar.** The end states are close to those of E64's permanent bar: gaps within 0.0002, rom_large within 0.0006, rom_middle within 0.003; E64's evaluation used its best-validation weights, 89,000 updates in s11. That is consistent with the bar acting mainly during the window; endpoint similarity cannot exclude effects in between. With E84 (the job left open while one head was held to pooling: the other head took the job in five of six) and E83 (a partner kept in three of four when no head held the job), these results support, without establishing as the unique mechanism, an early-allocation account: for these seeds, a head occupying the summaries job early keeps the net in B, rather than an inability to form or keep a second pooling head. In E37's ordinary training, the B lineages' second head takes that job.
- **For M2 (how they learn; why the B type deviates).** These results support the hypothesis that the B type is set early by an allocation event: whether one of the two block-1 heads occupies the summaries job. Removing that option through the first 10,000 updates sufficed for these six initialisations to form A's pair, which then persisted. This connects the head-allocation account (E63-E71, the head budget) to a training-time intervention on six seeds; whether the decision is irreversible or confined to this window is not tested.
- **Limits.**
  - Six seeds, all selected as B, and one bar length (10,000 updates).
  - The bar's permanent version (E64) was known to make these seeds A, so the new information is that the window suffices and the A allocation persists after the reopening.
  - The bar removes the summaries option from both heads at once, so which head would have taken the job, and whether a weaker bar suffices, are not tested.
  - The thresholds were set without dev runs, as the coordinator asked. Attention-mass criteria; end-of-schedule weights; CPU numerics.

## Update 97 (2026-11-02 22:54Z): E86, with E85's summaries bar lifted at 5,000 updates, five of six B initialisations still end A (P364: the registered rule's "supports D5"), namely the five whose heads had paired under the bar by 5,000 (P363); the sixth (s7), unpaired at 5,000, ends B with its roles swapped (amendment 94)

**TL;DR**
- **Design (CPU, training; coordinator-approved, at most 1 heavy process; registered before any run).** `train_nc.py --bar_until 5000` (E85's trainer and evaluation, unchanged) on E37's six B seeds: E64's summaries bar on both heads for updates 1-5,000, then pfn2's standard forward to 90,000.
  - Controls: E84's CPU retrains. Reference: E85 (the bar to 10,000).
  - The registered rule (P364) for D5, "the allocation is decided by 5,000 updates": A-converted in >= 4 of 6 supports it; <= 1 refutes it; 2-3 is undecided. The registration expected about 5 of 6, with s7 the likeliest exception, because E85's s7 had not paired by 5k.
- **P362 holds.** Step 0 equals E37's initial weights, and the 2k, 3k and 5k checkpoints equal E64's nocons checkpoints exactly, 6 of 6.
- **P363 holds (5 of 6).** At 5k, under the bar, both heads pool in s4, s5, s9, s10 and s11 (P_h 0.70-0.85, opposite-sign K). In s7 they do not (P_h 0.12/0.19; summaries mass 0.65/0.45, its self-attention allowed under the bar).
- **P364 supports D5 (5 of 6).** s4, s5, s9, s10 and s11 end A, with two opposite-sign pooling heads and rom_middle -0.035 to -0.052. s7 ends B: head 1 pools (P_h 0.80, K -1.70) and head 0 is on the summaries (0.98), the roles swapped relative to its control.
- **P365 holds (5 of 6).** gap(nc5) / gap(ctrl) is 0.43, 0.70, 0.52, 0.52 and 0.52 for the converted five, and 1.02 for s7.
- **P366 holds (5 of 6).** At 8k, both heads' summaries mass is at most 0.02 in the converted five; in s7 head 0's is 0.80.
- **Descriptive.** The five converted nets end close to E85's, though not identical to them: gaps within 0.0001, rom within 0.002, KLL 0.036-0.042 (E85 0.036-0.041), M3 0.073-0.083. s7's end state is an ordinary B net (KLL 0.130, M3 0.436). In s7, head 1 paired with the signed term by 8k (P_h 0.58, K -2.99) while head 0 stayed on the summaries; with E85's 10,000-update bar, s7's head 0 had become a pooler by 10k (P_h 0.62 under the bar).
- **What it shows.** By the registered rule (its operational criterion) this supports D5. A 5,000-update bar sufficed in the five seeds whose pair had formed under it, and those nets end close to E85's. s7, whose heads had not paired by 5,000, needed the tested 10,000-update bar: with the shorter bar, the head still mostly on the summaries took the reopened job. This is consistent with a seed-dependent stabilisation of the allocation. Two release times neither identify a decision window nor show that the commitment is irreversible, and the bar changes the whole learning trajectory. In E85 and E86, the seeds that had paired at the reopening kept the pair, and the one that had not ended B. That pairing is not necessary in general: in E84, s9 paired only after its release and still ended A. Six outcome-selected seeds; sufficiency, not mechanism; the 5k states were known from E85.
- **Review:** Codex (GPT-6, `gpt-6-astra`) asked for four fixes, all done (`results/review_e86.md`):
  - (high) the claim that pairing before the reopening goes with the outcome in every seed of E84-E86 has a counterexample (E84's s9 paired after its release and ended A): restricted to E85-E86, with s9 acknowledged and pairing not presented as necessary;
  - (high) "set by 5,000" and a seed-specific decision window exceeded two tested release times: now "a 5,000-update bar sufficed in five selected seeds and s7 needed the tested 10,000-update bar", consistent with seed-dependent stabilisation, with P364's "supports D5" kept as its operational rule;
  - (medium) "changed nothing measurable" conflicted with small nonzero differences from E85 (s11's gap 0.0080 against 0.0081, KLL 0.039 against 0.040), and sparse checkpoints cannot show continuous persistence: now "close to" and "retained at every later measured checkpoint";
  - (low) the benchmark's start and end times are now given separately, and the queue log is described as recording this lane's jobs, not a machine-wide census.
  It confirmed the hashes, the recipe and the bar through update 5,000, the identity checks, the strictly sequential jobs, the tables and the scoring of P362-P366.
- **Decision for Kelvin:** none.

**E86.2 Predictions**

| # | test | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| P362 | step 0 = E37's; 2k-5k = E64's nocons checkpoints, 6 of 6 | holds: 6 of 6 |
| P363 | under the bar at 5k both heads pool, >= 4 of 6 | holds: 5 of 6 (s7 not) |

| P366 | at 8k both heads' summaries mass < 0.5, >= 4 of 6 | holds: 5 of 6 (s7 0.80) |

**What this says.**
- **Two release times.** In five of six seeds the opposite-sign pair had formed under the bar by 5,000 updates. Lifting the bar then gave end states close to, but not identical with, a 10,000-update bar's (s11's gap 0.0080 against 0.0081; KLL 0.039 against 0.040), and the pair was retained at every later measured checkpoint.
- **The exception.** s7 had not paired by 5,000. When the job reopened, the head that was still mostly on the summaries took it, and the net ended B; with E85's longer bar it had paired by 10,000 and ended A. In E85 and E86, having paired at the reopening went with ending A in every seed. Pairing before the reopening is not necessary, though: E84's s9 paired after its release (own-token mass 0.28/0.29 at 10k, 0.60/0.61 at 11k) and ended A.
- **For M2 (how they learn).** Under this bar, a 5,000-update window sufficed in five seeds and s7 needed the 10,000-update one. This is consistent with an early, seed-dependent stabilisation of the allocation, which two bar lengths cannot time precisely.
- **Limits.** Six outcome-selected seeds and two bar lengths in total (E85, E86). The 5k states were known from E85 before registration (the runs repeat E85 exactly to 5,000). Sufficiency, not mechanism; attention-mass criteria; end-of-schedule weights.
